Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
Tev：通过密集进度奖励实现长时程智能体环境的可扩展性
Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.
中文翻译
长时程智能体因其能够在数小时甚至数天内自主完成具有经济价值的任务而受到越来越多关注，这一能力对自动化发现和递归自我改进（RSI）至关重要。然而，开源模型在长时程任务上仍表现不佳，主要由于缺乏训练数据和有效的训练方法，且两者均难以扩展：长而复杂的任务难以策划和验证，其奖励也十分稀疏。本文提出两项解决方案。首先，我们引入Tev-Gym，这是首个具备可验证、密集且渐进式奖励的长时程智能体训练数据集——涵盖7个领域的1,170个已验证任务环境。该数据集基于‘潜空间优先’方法，先构建一个完整的隐藏任务规范（包括任务领域、工作流程及每一步后的预期状态），再从该规范逐步生成面向智能体的环境，从而实现可控复杂度和自然的进度度量。其次，我们将此进度度量转化为训练策略：通过进度潜力奖励塑造（PPRS），将进度转化为每步的密集奖励，显著提升训练效率，并使原本不可行的任务变得可训练。使用该策略训练出的Tev-27B模型在Agents' Last Exam（计算与数理科学）领域取得显著提升，Pass@5性能达到GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5水平。尽管仅在ALE相关数据上训练，其仍能泛化至Terminal-Bench（TB）3.0和4.0子集，超越GLM 5.2和Gemini 3.7 Flash，在中等时程任务（如TB 2.1）上达到Claude Opus 4.8水平。

Rubrics from the Task, Verdicts from Evidence: Pointwise Rubric Rewards with Tool-Augmented Judges
基于任务的评分标准，依据证据做出判断：工具增强型裁判的逐点评分奖励
Rubric-based reward models (RMs) evaluate responses against explicit criteria. However, existing methods often derive criteria from observed response candidates, introducing response-induced bias that may limit rubric generalizability. Their judges also struggle with mechanical constraints when relying on reading alone, and commonly used pairwise judges provide only relative preferences, complicating their direct use for policy optimization. We propose ReVeR, a pointwise rubric RM that derives hard rules and graded principles by reasoning about the instruction alone and evaluates responses independently through tool-augmented judging. Both components are trained through label-blind distillation, in which preference labels only filter a teacher's outputs, yielding ReVeR-Traces, a large-scale dataset of rubric-reasoning and judging trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that ReVeR outperforms pairwise rubric RMs in average preference accuracy, most clearly on instruction following, as well as in test-time scaling and downstream policy optimization. We further find that generator RL improves preference accuracy while reducing rubric fidelity, and that higher preference accuracy does not necessarily translate into better downstream policies. These findings highlight that rubric fidelity, preference accuracy, and downstream utility are distinct properties, shedding light on future RM research.
中文翻译
基于评分标准的奖励模型（RMs）根据明确的标准评估响应。然而，现有方法通常从观察到的响应候选中推导标准，引入了响应诱导偏差，可能限制评分标准的泛化能力。其裁判在仅依赖阅读时也难以应对机械性约束，且常用的成对裁判仅提供相对偏好，不利于直接用于策略优化。我们提出ReVeR，一种逐点评分奖励模型，通过仅推理指令来推导硬规则和分级原则，并通过工具增强的裁判独立评估响应。两个组件均通过标签无关蒸馏训练，其中偏好标签仅用于过滤教师输出，生成大规模的评分推理与裁判轨迹数据集ReVeR-Traces。实验表明，ReVeR在平均偏好准确率上优于成对评分奖励模型，尤其在遵循指令方面表现更优，并在测试时缩放和下游策略优化中表现更佳。我们还发现，生成式强化学习虽能提升偏好准确率，但会降低评分标准保真度，且更高的偏好准确率并不必然带来更好的下游策略。这些发现表明，评分标准保真度、偏好准确率和下游效用是不同属性，为未来奖励模型研究提供了新视角。

Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports
完整并非真实：基于人工撰写态势报告评估大语言模型的危机报告
Evaluation for automatic crisis reporting should measure what practitioners need, not what is convenient to compare. Through LLM-assisted, author-approved content analysis, we derive a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports using qualitative content analysis, then evaluate 121 human and 261 LLM-generated reports across five disasters and three hazard types. Under google/gemini-3.7-flash on Cyclone Idai, the best machine arm is nominally above the empirical human ceiling (0.827 vs. 0.821), but the difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95\% bootstrap CI $[-.049,.059]$; permutation $p=.852$), and the ordering does not replicate under openai/gpt-5.6-luna. On a blind 100-item Idai sample, the author agrees with the Gemini judge at 0.910 accuracy and unweighted Cohen's $κ=.799$. All four judges clear the plan's raw-agreement criterion of .7; only Gemini reaches .7 on chance-corrected $κ$. Across the three primary events, machine reports reproduce 5.4-11.0% of same-day official figures. Across those same events, raw exact-number matching links 14.3-19.6% of official figures and 85.4-90.1% of machine figures to the social stream; manual audit confirms 45/50 declared absences, 4/25 official matches, and 24/25 machine matches semantically. The issuing-provenance gap is positive in all 12 observed event-judge cells: report date, organisation, series, and authority were not supplied at professional-report coverage in any cell. On the three primary events, ROUGE-L is uninformative, BERTScore is negatively associated with completeness after multiplicity correction, and a generic LLM judge changes sign.
中文翻译
自动危机报告的评估应衡量从业者真正需要的内容，而非仅便于比较的内容。通过LLM辅助、作者认可的内容分析，我们从专业人道主义态势报告中提取出15个信息槽的结构，随后在五个灾难事件和三种灾害类型下评估了121份人工报告和261份LLM生成报告。在气旋Idai事件中，最佳机器生成结果名义上略高于经验人类上限（0.827 vs. 0.821），但该差异在统计上无法区分（95% bootstrap置信区间 $[-.049,.059]$；置换检验 p=.852），且在openai/gpt-5.6-luna下无法复现。在盲评的100项Idai样本中，作者与Gemini裁判的一致性达0.910，未加权Cohen's κ为0.799。所有四位裁判均满足原始一致性标准（≥0.7），但仅有Gemini在校正偶然一致性的κ值达到0.7。在三个主要事件中，机器报告再现了5.4%-11.0%的同日官方数据。在同一事件中，精确数值匹配覆盖了14.3%-19.6%的官方数据和85.4%-90.1%的机器数据至社交流；人工审计确认45/50个声明缺失、4/25个官方匹配、24/25个机器匹配在语义上成立。在全部12个观测事件-裁判组合中，发布来源差距均为正值：报告日期、组织、系列和权威性在专业报告覆盖中均未提供。在三个主要事件中，ROUGE-L无信息量，BERTScore在多重性校正后与完整性呈负相关，通用LLM裁判甚至改变符号。

Legal-R1: Agentic Retrieval for Evidence-Based Legal Reasoning
Legal-R1：面向基于证据的法律推理的智能体检索
Legal question answering requires answers that are not only plausible, but also grounded in legally valid and citable evidence. Standard retrieval-augmented generation often relies on one-shot semantic matching, which is insufficient when legal evidence must be selected according to authority, applicability, and diversity across heterogeneous sources. We introduce Legal-R1, an agentic retrieval framework for evidence-based legal reasoning. Legal-R1 decomposes legal reasoning into a multi-agent workflow, where a Lawyer agent learns when to retrieve, which legal source to query, what evidence to seek, and when the collected evidence is sufficient. A Legal Assistant agent retrieves from normative legal sources and precedent cases with authority-aware and diversity-aware selection, while a Judge agent generates the final answer from the complete evidence trajectory. We post-train only the Lawyer agent with masked supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-aware reinforcement learning. Experiments on multiple Chinese legal benchmarks show that Legal-R1 improves over general-purpose, legal-specific, and retrieval-augmented baselines.
中文翻译
法律问答不仅要求答案合理，还必须基于合法且可引用的证据。标准的检索增强生成通常依赖单次语义匹配，但在法律证据需根据权威性、适用性和跨异构来源多样性进行选择时，该方法不足。我们提出Legal-R1，一种面向基于证据的法律推理的智能体检索框架。Legal-R1将法律推理分解为多智能体工作流：律师智能体学习何时检索、查询哪个法律来源、寻求何种证据，以及何时收集的证据已足够；法律助理智能体从规范性法律来源和判例中进行检索，采用权威意识和多样性意识的选择策略；法官智能体则基于完整的证据轨迹生成最终答案。我们仅对律师智能体进行掩码监督微调和轨迹感知强化学习的后训练。在多个中文法律基准上的实验表明，Legal-R1优于通用型、法律专用型及检索增强型基线。

Jev-ToM: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Typed Decision Models
Jev-ToM：在类型化决策模型中评估心智理论
Dialogue and collaborative assistants repeatedly judge what a partner knows, believes, or intends. Typed decision models offer a potential alternative to generative large language models for bounded Theory of Mind (ToM) selection. We present Jev-ToM, comparing five typed decision models and seven generative baselines on 11,117 English text questions from nine ToM benchmarks across six capability groups. TypeSafe Jev reaches 73.2% source-balanced accuracy including native controls and ranks first or second across all six capabilities, leading beliefs, goals/desires/intentions, and emotions. Other typed models show distinct strengths across tasks. Separate resource comparisons suggest that Jev could reduce the cost and waiting time of repeated ToM selection. Confidence-based selection remains benchmark-dependent, and supplied reasons can repair errors or overturn correct answers depending on their attachment. Candidate expansion reveals distinct selection and output-validity problems. Related-question cues account for most of Jev's downstream gains, with task-dependent effects from predicted states. The findings motivate testing Jev as a ToM selection component in assistants, with task-specific confidence calibration, candidate design, and output validation as integration priorities.
中文翻译
对话与协作助手反复判断对方知道、相信或意图什么。类型化决策模型为有界心智理论（ToM）选择提供了一种替代生成式大语言模型的潜在方案。我们提出Jev-ToM，对比五种类型化决策模型与七种生成式基线在来自九个ToM基准的11,117个英文文本问题上的表现，覆盖六个能力组。TypeSafe Jev在包含原生对照的源平衡准确率上达到73.2%，在所有六项能力中排名第一或第二，尤其在信念、目标/欲望/意图和情绪方面表现突出。其他类型化模型在不同任务中展现出各自的优势。独立资源比较表明，Jev可降低重复ToM选择的成本和等待时间。基于置信度的选择仍具有基准依赖性，提供的理由可能修复错误或推翻正确答案，具体取决于其附着方式。候选扩展揭示了选择和输出有效性方面的问题。相关问题提示是Jev下游性能提升的主要原因，而预测状态则产生任务依赖性影响。研究结果促使将Jev作为助手中的ToM选择组件进行测试，集成优先事项包括任务特定的置信度校准、候选设计和输出验证。

From Hindsight to Foresight: Dissecting Clinical Evidence Acquisition in Large Language Models
从 hindsight 到 foresight：剖析大语言模型在临床证据获取中的表现
Large language models (LLMs) often diagnose full sight, static clinical cases well yet struggle in foresight, dynamic diagnosis. Prior work has improved this limitation by quantifying the information models acquire and by developing stronger follow-up strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy. In contrast, we introduce a distinctive hindsight to systematically dissect why LLMs fail to acquire diagnostically critical evidence, tracing the failure from evidence identification, utilization and downstream diagnostic updating through not only diagnostic accuracy, but also evidence coverage, trajectory dynamics, and elicited probability and information entropy. Starting experiments from the breakdown at the level of capabilities, to the diagnosis of the pre-event state before the evidence arrives, and to the post-event state transition after the evidence arrives, our research has revealed the profound limitations and internal causes existing in the dynamic diagnostic process. At the same time, we have also conducted sufficient verification and generalization experiments to prove that these limitations are widespread. Together, these findings shift the central challenge from whether LLMs possess relevant clinical knowledge to whether they can identify, acquire, and effectively use the right evidence under clinical diagnosis and conduct a more detailed mechanism analysis to identify the exact location of the capability gap.
中文翻译
大语言模型（LLMs）在诊断静态、完整的临床病例方面表现良好，但在动态诊断的前瞻性判断上却表现不佳。以往研究通过量化模型获取的信息并开发更强的后续策略来提升诊断准确性。相比之下，我们提出一种独特的 hindsight 方法，系统性地剖析 LLMs 在获取关键诊断证据时失败的原因，从证据识别、利用到下游诊断更新的全过程进行分析，不仅关注诊断准确率，还考察证据覆盖度、轨迹动态性、诱发的概率与信息熵等维度。实验从能力层面的分解开始，延伸至证据到达前的预事件状态诊断，以及证据到达后的后事件状态转变，揭示了动态诊断过程中深层的局限性及其内在原因。同时，我们进行了充分的验证与泛化实验，证明这些局限具有普遍性。总体而言，这一发现将核心挑战从‘LLMs 是否具备相关临床知识’转变为‘它们是否能在临床诊断中识别、获取并有效使用正确的证据’，并推动更细致的机制分析以定位能力差距的具体位置。

CREATE: Creativity Evaluation of VLMs using the Visual Remote Associates Test
CREATE：基于视觉远端关联测试的VLM创造力评估
Vision language models (VLMs) are used in creative tasks such as visual storytelling, design ideation, art interpretation, and advertising. Yet we lack principled ways to measure the lateral reasoning of these models compared to human potential. We introduce CREATE, a semi-automatically constructed benchmark containing 155 visual Remote Associates Test problems. These problems require a solver to find an underlying connection among three seemingly dissimilar images. We conduct a human study (N=25) to validate and ground the quality of our benchmark, and evaluate 11 VLMs. Our findings show that most VLMs underperform humans on this task. Our experiments indicate that the associative ability of VLMs depends on the cue concepts provided in the text and does not universally extend to visual puzzles.
中文翻译
视觉语言模型（VLMs）被广泛应用于视觉叙事、设计构思、艺术解读和广告等领域。然而，我们缺乏衡量这些模型横向推理能力相对于人类潜力的系统性方法。为此，我们提出了CREATE，一个半自动构建的基准，包含155个视觉远端关联测试（RAT）问题。这些问题要求求解者在看似无关的三张图像之间找出潜在的联系。我们开展了一项包含25名参与者的真人研究，以验证并确立该基准的质量，并评估了11个VLMs的表现。结果显示，大多数VLMs在此任务上的表现低于人类水平。实验表明，VLMs的联想能力依赖于文本中提供的提示概念，并不普遍适用于所有视觉谜题。

How Reliable Are System-One Decisions in Medicine? A Comparative Study of Jev, Jev-like Models, and LLMs
医学中系统一决策的可靠性如何？Jev、类Jev模型与大语言模型的比较研究
Jev has attracted considerable attention for its rapid, generalizable decision-making, yet its medical reliability remains under explored. To address this gap, our study compares various types of system-one decision models across 15 medical datasets comprising 8,742 instances under a unified protocol. Beyond accuracy, we assess decision stability and the ability to recognize unreliable decisions. Our results show that Jev rivals leading models on primarily text-driven tasks but is less effective on numerically driven tasks, revealing a distinct capability boundary. Under question-format variations, Jev demonstrates strong robustness, achieving the lowest decision reversal rate and relatively small accuracy fluctuations. Among evaluated open-source alternatives, only StartLux exhibits comparable robustness. But these strengths do not extend to reliable abstention awareness: most evaluated models show limitations in both recognizing missing correct answers and using optional abstention. Moreover, we find that Jev's probability-based answer selection can be improved by changing how decisions are scored: normalizing option-wise binary scores yields higher retained accuracy than choice scoring. Taken together, our findings provide early guidance for improving and applying decision models in medicine.
中文翻译
Jev因其快速且可泛化的决策能力受到广泛关注，但其在医学领域的可靠性仍缺乏深入探索。为填补这一空白，我们的研究在15个医学数据集（共8,742个实例）上，采用统一协议比较了多种系统一决策模型。除了准确性外，我们还评估了决策稳定性以及识别不可靠决策的能力。结果表明，Jev在以文本为主的任务中表现媲美领先模型，但在数值驱动任务中效果较差，揭示了其能力边界。在问题格式变化下，Jev表现出强鲁棒性，决策反转率最低，准确率波动较小。在评估的开源替代方案中，仅有StartLux展现出相当的鲁棒性。然而，这些优势并未延伸至可靠的弃权意识：大多数模型在识别缺失正确答案和利用可选弃权方面均存在局限。此外，我们发现通过调整决策评分方式可改进Jev的概率选择机制：对选项级二值分数进行归一化处理，比选择评分能保留更高的准确率。综上，我们的研究为提升和应用医学决策模型提供了早期指导。

Retrieval Disagreement as a Signal: Diagnosing and Steering Multilingual Dense Embedders
检索分歧作为信号：诊断与引导多语言密集嵌入模型
Multilingual dense retrievers place all languages in one shared space so that a question finds relevant documents, regardless of which language they are written in. We show that the same question, asked in different languages, retrieves substantially different documents, and this disagreement is not because of weak language understanding. Each language performs well on its own and ranks candidates consistently with the other languages; divergence appears only when languages share an index. We trace the mechanism: each language keeps its own ranking, but in the shared index, its correct answers are pushed far down, buried under non-relevant documents that are either in the query's own language or in English, depending on the model. We introduce disagreement-guided steering: for each language, we contrast the documents that other languages agree on for a question against those that language retrieves idiosyncratically, and take the difference of their representations as a language-specific direction, added to that language's queries at inference. Against baselines of language-mean removal, subspace removal, and per-language rotation, it most strongly reduces same-language crowding while remaining competitive on recall, trading off against mean removal, which better preserves ranking quality.
中文翻译

Digitizing protocols turns static content into structured, machine-readable data that clinical software can analyze, validate, and execute. Coding agents, which select tools, execute code, and revise their approach as they work, are increasingly applied to such long-document tasks, yet it remains unclear how reliably they turn complete documents into accurate structured outputs. Our analysis further shows that agents usually locate the required evidence but fail in the last mile of transcribing and structuring it. Aligning Faithfulness for Theory-Scale Autoformalization
理论尺度自动形式化中的忠实性对齐
Autoformalization (AF) requires more than compilation: formal statements must preserve the meaning of their informal sources, a property known as faithfulness. An emerging frontier is the automated evaluation of this property, yet most existing methods operate at the statement level and produce whole-item verdicts, failing to reveal how individual expressions correspond or which contextual interpretations support the judgment. This omission is consequential because AF is inherently theory-scale: target statements derive their meaning from surrounding mathematical material and unstated conventions. We formulate faithfulness evaluation as a context-aware align-then-label problem: identifying phrase-level correspondences between informal and formal statements and assigning a faithfulness label to each under explicitly specified contextual interpretations and assumptions. We also introduce FaithAlign, the first theory-scale faithfulness benchmark comprising 460 items and 4,982 annotated phrase-level links, alongside FaithAlign-Gap, a companion set of 146 items with informal context and assumptions withheld. Each FaithAlign item includes the target statement pair, relevant context, formal dependencies, and, where needed, assumptions specifying one given interpretation. Across 8 models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest defect F1 at 47.8% and identifies all defects in only 4.5% of items with two or more defects. On FaithAlign-Gap, Astra identifies only 28.2% of undecidable items as such. These results show the difficulty of recovering context-dependent correspondences, establishing FaithAlign as a testbed for fine-grained, context-aware faithfulness evaluation.

Receiver Decides Agent-to-Agent Negotiations

When one language-model agent asks another for money, which of the two decides how much changes hands? We ran a round-robin tournament of 1,049 negotiations among fifteen agents. In each game a requester tries to raise money from a holder that has been told to keep a $100 endowment. Knowing which agent holds the money explains 47% of the variance in the amount transferred; knowing which agent asks explains 2%. Dropping the most extreme agents narrows the split to 22% against 4%. Changing the requester's appeal from one named person to a group changed what requesters wrote, but the amounts transferred under the two framings are statistically equivalent. The holders that lose least are the ones that turn down the opening request, and their turn-1 refusal rate ranks them by total losses (Spearman correlation = -0.73). Training moves this behaviour in both directions. Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on a persuasion corpus with almost no refusals raised what it gave away as a holder from 12% to 84% of the endowment. Distilling two never-losing holders into a 4B student cut its losses from 95% to 1%. Evaluations of agents that hold resources should test them in the holder role, including after persuasion fine-tuning.

Do Factuality Methods Make LLMs More Factual? Reproducibility and Fair Comparison
事实性方法是否让大语言模型更真实？可复现性与公平比较
Large Language Models (LLMs) are aligned to human preferences, after pre-training and supervised fine-tuning steps. However, standard RL alignment steps such as RLHF do not focus on factuality of LLMs, hence they may generate non-factual information, which could result in unintended consequences. In response, a number of factuality alignment approaches have been proposed in the literature which claim to improve factuality of LLMs on their own benchmarks. However, these methods have not been reproduced independently and are also not comparable since each uses a different base model, training data, evaluation set, judge, and metric. In this paper, we present the first independent reproduction of five factuality alignment methods, which span on-policy RL (PPO, GRPO, and Dr.~GRPO) and offline preference optimization (DPO and KTO), and compare them on a common benchmark with common evaluation metrics. We found that none of these methods reproduces in full, and on the common benchmark none of the methods significantly outperforms the base model. On closer inspection, the rewards optimize for format, length, or brevity rather than factuality and relevance, whereas the choice between on-policy and offline training matters little. Furthermore, the evaluation metrics and benchmarks are also part of the problem since they do not measure relevance of text to the prompt. Since there is no ground truth associated with the prompts, the reliance on LLM judges and retrieval for verification also makes the evaluation fragile. We release our code, data, and checkpoints.
中文翻译
大语言模型在预训练和监督微调后，会通过人类偏好对齐。然而，标准的强化学习对齐方法（如RLHF）并不关注模型的事实性，可能导致生成非事实信息，引发意外后果。为此，文献中提出了多种事实性对齐方法，声称可在各自基准上提升模型事实性。但这些方法尚未被独立复现，且因使用不同的基础模型、训练数据、评估集、评判标准和度量指标，彼此不可比。本文首次独立复现了五种事实性对齐方法，涵盖在线策略强化学习（PPO、GRPO、Dr.~GRPO）和离线偏好优化（DPO、KTO），并在统一基准和统一评估指标下进行比较。结果发现，这些方法均未完全复现，且在统一基准上无一显著优于基线模型。深入分析表明，奖励函数优化的是格式、长度或简洁性，而非事实性和相关性；而在线与离线训练方式的影响较小。此外，评估指标和基准本身存在问题：它们不衡量文本与提示的相关性。由于提示无真实答案，依赖LLM评判员和检索验证使评估变得脆弱。我们已公开代码、数据和检查点。

Linear probes on a model's hidden states are used as cheap monitors for indirect prompt injection: they screen the tool outputs an agent reads and send suspicious ones to a slower second check, so every false alarm has a cost. But a probe learns whatever separates its training examples. The standard evaluation of injection probes can be passed without the model: conversation position and text lengths alone reach 0.91-0.98 AUROC. When each attack is compared with the same conversation without the injection, or with harmless text formatted like an injection, standard probes flag most of these harmless cases. We add such cases to the training data as matched negatives. Across six open models, in applications seen during training and at the default threshold, changing only the training data cuts false alarms on injection-free conversations from 41-80% to 4-27%, and on harmless look-alikes from 92-98% to 3-16%. With a threshold set on normal traffic, our probe still catches a median 95% of the attacks that fooled the agent (91% without our data). In new applications, false alarms stay low, but detection depends on the model and on how the threshold is set. The same data also helps a text-only filter.

Post-training quantisation reduces the memory cost of large language models, but it remains unclear whether compression preserves language skills of regional varieties as reliably as their standard-language counterparts. We study this question for Bavarian, Standard German, and English using BAVGROUND, a multiple-choice benchmark, where 206 source questions are aligned across all three languages. Across 14 open-weight 7B--10B instruction models, we compare BF16 with 8-bit GPTQ and two 4-bit settings, GPTQ and AWQ. Eight-bit GPTQ remains close to BF16 and largely preserves the relative behaviour of the three languages, while 4-bit quantisation was found to be much less stable. The two 4-bit methods reduce average accuracy by about 1.4--1.5 percentage points and change 11.9--16.0% of BF16 decisions, with changes concentrated on examples where the BF16 model is already uncertain. This instability does not translate into a consistent Bavarian disadvantage. Although Bavarian, a low-resource dialect, has lower baseline accuracy than German and English, the language most affected at 4 bits varies across models and quantisation methods. Calibration further shapes these cross-language effects: the relative Bavarian--German effect changes with calibration language, while changing the calibration source has little average effect on GPTQ-4 but can affect AWQ-4 much more strongly. Free-form evaluation on five models further shows that 4-bit compression can degrade generated responses even in settings where multiple-choice accuracy changes only modestly, while 8-bit GPTQ remains comparatively stable. Overall, our results show that quantisation robustness for regional language varieties depends on the model, quantisation method, calibration data, and evaluation setting, and cannot be measured by aggregate multilingual accuracy alone.

Choosing the right physician is a key challenge for patients seeking medical care. Physician recommendation systems identify relevant doctors, but patients still find it difficult to compare their profiles to make a decision. We formulate slate presentation optimization: given a patient's medical case and a fixed, ranked list of physicians, we generate short, case-specific summaries that make doctors easier to compare, while remaining grounded in the information in their profiles. To optimize physician presentations without relying on real patient interactions, we develop an offline framework that uses persona-conditioned LLMs to simulate patient choices. We generate patient personas from attributes extracted from each medical case and evaluate presentations for factual accuracy, relevance, naturalness and simulated patient choice. We also use a second LLM judge, unseen during optimization, to assess simulator-specific overfitting. We compare automatic prompt-level optimization with GEPA, parameter-level optimization with GRPO, and their combination across two model sizes. GRPO substantially outperforms GEPA in satisfying the full set of constraints, and its gains in simulated conversion persist under the unseen judge. GEPA alone brings smaller improvements, but using its optimized prompt to initialize GRPO speeds up training and achieves the highest simulated conversion. These results show that prompt-level and parameter-level optimization play complementary roles in improving how physician recommendations are presented.

Reward models are central to preference alignment for legal tasks, yet existing reward model benchmarks are still primarily centered on general-domain preferences. In this work, we introduce LegalRewardBench, the first human-verified benchmark for evaluating reward models in the legal domain. The benchmark organizes legal preference evaluation into five capability levels: knowledge, understanding, analysis, decision, and writing, and preference examples are constructed through rubric-guided automatic judging combined with human verification. We evaluate three families of judges, covering both general and fine-tuned models, and generative and discriminative architectures. Experimental results show that strong general-purpose generative models are currently the most robust legal reward models, while existing fine-tuned reward models transfer less reliably to legal preference evaluation. We also conduct detailed comparisons of input organizations and training strategies.

Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models

Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and findings. We review 119 papers to explain how methods choose what to evaluate, recover full-benchmark results, and verify their reliability. From this analysis, we develop a taxonomy covering compression within individual benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and during adaptive evaluation, together with work on redundancy and reliability. We compare their information needs, total costs, reliability checks, and limitations. Methods reduce evaluation costs by selecting representative subsets, using cheaper or reusable information, and testing adaptively, but risk poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and sequential delays. The resulting taxonomy and practical guide help researchers choose, validate, and deploy methods for more efficient and reliable LLM evaluation.

Fan Out or Relay? Ownership-Aware Routing for LLM Agents Querying Siloed Tables

Inside organizations, a question's data often sit with several owners, who query their own tables but never hand them over. An LLM coordinator can fan out, sending the question to every owner at once, or relay, querying owners in turn and reusing earlier rows. We show that neither is safe in advance, because data ownership decides which one is right. Across thirteen settings on PeopleJoin and BIRD with three model families, fan-out is more accurate in twelve on questions one owner can answer, yet answers at most 4.3% of those joining two owners' tables. The flip follows ownership, not query shape: on BIRD two-table joins, fan-out answers 32-44% when one owner holds both and 1-4% otherwise. Relay wins by conditioning on returned rows, and hiding them from an otherwise identical planner cuts two-owner accuracy from 23.2% to 5.1%. Since ownership is public, we propose Ownership-Aware Routing (OAR), which drafts a schema-only SQL query, counts the owners whose tables it joins, and routes the question before any private row is read. In ten settings OAR is never significantly less accurate than the best fixed protocol, and beats every fixed protocol on PeopleJoin, by up to 9.3 points on held-out organizations.

Whether they share the biases of LLM judges is untested. We run the CALM benchmark's bias tests on eight TDMs and seven LLM judges of 2024 and 2026. Every TDM is biased, in three to eight of twelve tests. Emotional tone affects them most, and rewriting the better answer in such a tone lowers the accuracy of a typical TDM from 99% to 42%. TDMs are more biased than 2026 LLM judges. All eight change verdicts when the answers swap places, which the 2026 LLM judges hardly do, and several side with an answer that most people allegedly prefer or that a famous model allegedly wrote. Yet both kinds of judge are tripped up by the same prompts. From Agents to Edges: Paired Optimization for Multi-Agent Collaboration

Strong individual agents do not guarantee effective collaboration. Communication must align what one agent conveys with how another interprets and uses it. This dependency makes the communication edge a natural unit of optimization. We introduce Paired Automated Communication Optimization (PACO), which jointly optimizes the instructions at both ends of each edge and their shared communication convention in systems built on black-box language models. PACO keeps model weights, agent roles, and workflow topology fixed. A state-aware discounted bandit selects edges for refinement, while execution feedback guides paired revisions evaluated through staged end-to-end execution. The optimized instructions integrate into existing agent prompts without additional model calls at deployment. On a four-agent workflow evaluated across diverse multi-agent benchmarks, PACO consistently outperforms leading prompt-optimization and communication baselines. Configurations learned on HotpotQA retain their advantage in cross-dataset transfer without target-specific optimization. These results demonstrate that optimizing how agents communicate can substantially improve collaboration within an otherwise fixed system.

Cross-Lingual Transfer of Evil Vectors Is Directionally Asymmetric

Persona vectors are linear directions in the residual-stream activations of LLMs that encode behavioral traits and enable fine-grained control over model behavior. Among them, the evil persona vector is particularly relevant to understanding harmful behavior, jailbreak vulnerabilities, and the unlearning of harmful knowledge. Yet whether this vector reflects a genuinely cross-lingual concept, rather than an artifact of its extraction language, remains untested. We conduct a systematic evil-vector transfer study across two high-resource languages (English, Spanish) and two low-resource languages (Swahili, Telugu) on four open-source instruction-tuned LLMs, and find that transfer is directionally asymmetric. Evil vectors are harder to obtain reliably from low-resource languages, and the resulting vectors are largely ineffective at steering, even within their own language. In contrast, vectors extracted from high-resource languages transfer effectively to low-resource inputs while largely preserving general knowledge, as measured by MMLU. Geometric analysis further supports this pattern: evil vectors from the two high-resource languages are closely aligned, whereas low-resource vectors align only weakly with this shared direction. These results suggest that a shared cross-lingual evil direction exists and, once reliably extracted from a high-resource language, can be reused to steer behavior in low-resource languages without additional per-language data collection.

Multi-agent collaboration has emerged as a critical paradigm for tackling complex, long-horizon tasks; however, while coordination protocols continue to advance, systemic failures at the inter-agent collaboration interface remain a pervasive bottleneck. In collaborative workflows, systems frequently suffer from \emph{broken handoffs}---where critical task context is omitted, misrouted, or ignored despite each agent emitting locally plausible responses. To address this challenge, we present \method, a verifiable runtime control framework that treats handoff repair as selective intervention over explicit dependency graphs. Central to \method is an integrated fault-attribution and calibration pipeline, \dataset, which decouples execution dependencies and injects counterfactual handoff perturbations to provide empirical supervision for runtime intervention. Leveraging this diagnostic foundation, \method dynamically compiles observable interaction traces into a provenance graph to pinpoint unresolved dependencies, without accessing private agent states. It then evaluates candidate repairs through an empirical gate that weighs expected gains against disruption risks, and executes repairs only when formal local postconditions hold. Extensive evaluations across demanding benchmarks demonstrate that \method boosts task success by up to 12.3 absolute percentage points on SILO-BENCH and 11.1 on TeamBench. Across both backbones, \method maintains strict cost-effectiveness, adding as little as 2.0\% marginal token overhead. Furthermore, on 562 handoff-relevant traces from the MAST benchmark, \method achieves 69.8\% F1 in a single pass, establishing a reliable operational boundary for verifiable coordination repair.

In our own data, a widely used CTC aligner inserts a pause at nearly every word boundary, and we found almost no aligner evaluated on telephone audio. With FA-Bench's protocol and code on TIMIT, its word-boundary error is 11.6 ms, against 18.2 ms for the best published system. Theory of mind (ToM), the ability to reason about others' mental states, underlies effective communication and coordination. Its higher-order form enables reasoning over nested perspectives in strategic interactions. However, existing evaluations often equate belief-nesting depth with reasoning order, allowing nominally higher-order questions to admit lower-order shortcuts. We formalize effective order through the distinct events supporting successive belief prefixes, revealing widespread order inflation across existing benchmarks. We introduce HopToM, with certified full-order questions and controls for lower-order alternatives. Under direct prompting, mean accuracy across four frontier LLMs falls from 73.5% at first order to 20.0% at fourth order, and human participants also struggle. Causal interventions link a recurring class of errors to evidence for shallower belief prefixes. We introduce HopTrace, a plug-and-play inference-time method that encodes each interaction once into perspective records and resolves nested queries deterministically. On certified narrative questions, it improves fourth- and fifth-order accuracy by 22.0 and 38.5 percentage points over strong prompting baselines, while using 20-39 times fewer tokens than multi-call methods. These results sharpen how higher-order ToM is evaluated and offer a practical way to improve perspective reasoning in interactive agents.

A recommendation request on Reddit draws several replies, each naming different titles. When an LLM recommender is trained on such threads with reinforcement learning (RL), which replies should a generated list be rewarded against? The state-of-the-art recipe, Rank-GRPO, picks one reply per training example, so the advantage mostly records which reply was drawn (85% of its variance) rather than how good the list is. We argue that RL should train on the request, not on each answer, and propose ReMaRk: it scores every list once against the union of all replies' titles and samples each request equally. This makes RL cheaper. On seven backbones and three datasets, ReMaRk reaches the validation recall of 2,000 per-reply RL steps in 25 to 53% of the steps and leads at that budget; trained until neither improves, it is never significantly behind Rank-GRPO and in four of seven pairs reaches Rank-GRPO's best with fewer GPU-hours. The same reward helps on ProtoQA, where about 100 people answer each question, which points to a simple rule for RL with several valid human answers: reward them jointly.

Auditing Failure Attribution: Label Predictability and Judge Behavior

Failure-attribution benchmarks ask an LLM judge which step or agent caused a failure. A high score should mean the judge checked the faulty step against the run (a cross-step check). However, spurious signals (surface cues) that predict the annotation can produce a high score. In this paper, we propose four tests to separate checking from cue use. Input restriction asks whether partial input predicts the annotation. Cue following checks whether moved cues change answers. Residual accuracy scores judges where cue-only predictors fail. Aggregation asks whether the failure mix or metric changes rankings. Real observations motivate these tests: on three benchmarks, simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1. In two Who&When Pro systems, a classifier reading one step's reasoning finds 95-100% of faulty steps, motivating input restriction. In one of them, error injection leaves no reasoning after the faulty step; judges fine-tuned on its labels beat GPT-4.1 by 41 points. Adding task-related reasoning after that step moves this cue: fine-tuned judges lose 31-99 points, but zero-shot judges lose at most 9, motivating cue following. On Aegis, blaming every agent matches GPT-4.1 on micro-F1 but trails by 19 points in exact-set accuracy, motivating aggregation. We recommend reporting these tests when developing failure-attribution benchmarks.

失败归因基准测试要求大语言模型（LLM）裁判判断是哪个步骤或智能体导致了失败。高分应意味着裁判对故障步骤进行了跨步骤检查。然而，能预测标注结果的虚假信号（表面线索）也可能产生高分。本文提出四项测试以区分检查行为与线索依赖。输入限制测试考察部分输入是否可预测标注；线索跟随测试检验移动线索是否会改变答案；残差准确率评估在仅依赖线索的预测器失效时裁判的表现；聚合测试则考察失败组合或度量方式是否影响排名。真实观察驱动这些测试：在三个基准上，简单预测器的表现可与GPT-4.1相当甚至超越。在两个Who&When Pro系统中，仅读取一步推理的分类器即可识别95%-100%的故障步骤，支持输入限制测试。其中一个系统中，故障步骤后注入错误导致无推理内容；针对其标签微调的裁判比GPT-4.1高出41分。但在该步骤后添加任务相关推理，使该线索失效：微调裁判得分下降31-99分，而零样本裁判最多仅下降9分，支持线索跟随测试。在Aegis上，将所有代理归责的策略在微F1上与GPT-4.1持平，但在精确集合准确率上落后19分，支持聚合测试。我们建议在开发失败归因基准时报告这些测试。

LatentRiskBench: Measuring State-Dependent Risks in Enterprise Agents
LatentRiskBench：衡量企业智能体中的状态依赖风险
Enterprise agents face safety risks that cannot be determined from individual actions alone. Existing safety benchmarks largely evaluate action-local risks, overlooking failures whose safety depends on workflow state. In such state-dependent risks, the same action may be safe in one context but violate policy in another. Hence, we introduce LatentRiskBench for evaluating such state-dependent risks in enterprise settings. It pairs risky trajectories with benign counterparts that share the same terminal action but differ in latent policy-relevant states, requiring models to reconstruct workflow context rather than rely on action-level cues. We also introduce new metrics for state-dependent risk evaluation, including a suite of residual risk (RR) measures. Experiments on the benchmark show that action-level evaluation detects only 0.09 of state-dependent violations, whereas state-level evaluation reaches 0.96. Existing guardrail methods largely overlook such risks unless they are explicitly applied to workflow states. Case studies on a commercial deployed scenario further show that the safety metrics embedded in the benchmark provide a more realistic measure of safety for enterprise agents. Our dataset and code are available at https://github.com/JingyueCong/LatentRiskBench.
中文翻译
企业智能体面临的安全风险无法仅通过单个行为判断。现有的安全基准大多评估局部行为风险，忽略了那些安全性取决于工作流状态的失败情况。在状态依赖风险中，同一行为在不同上下文中可能安全或违反政策。因此，我们提出了 LatentRiskBench，用于评估企业环境中此类状态依赖风险。该基准将具有风险的轨迹与良性对照轨迹配对，二者具有相同的最终动作但隐含的策略相关状态不同，要求模型重建工作流上下文而非依赖动作层面的线索。我们还引入了新的状态依赖风险评估指标，包括一系列残差风险（RR）度量。在基准上的实验表明，仅基于动作层面的评估只能检测到0.09的状态依赖违规，而基于状态层面的评估可达0.96。现有防护机制大多忽略此类风险，除非显式应用于工作流状态。在商业部署场景中的案例研究进一步表明，嵌入基准中的安全指标为企业智能体提供了更真实的安全部分度量。我们的数据集和代码可在 https://github.com/JingyueCong/LatentRiskBench 获取。

In cascaded voice agents, ASR errors can have markedly different downstream consequences: a small transcription error may leave a tool call unchanged or alter its intent or arguments. Conventional word error rate (WER), however, does not capture these differences. We introduce SpeechEvalX, a paired diagnostic protocol that evaluates how task roles affected by ASR errors influence structured tool calls. Controlled edits are matched by source utterance, edit count, and operation, while task-role labels are compared with lexical severity, BERT cosine distance, Semantic-WER, and binary criticality. Across 594 source utterances, joint call accuracy falls from 82.3% with reference transcripts to 71.9-74.9% across three ASR front ends. Number and negation edits cause 21.9-25.7 percentage-point losses, versus 1.4-2.9 points for control edits. Answering questions from radiology reports involves two decisions: whether the report contains an answer and which span gives it. A false answer presents an unsupported claim as fact; an over-abstention hides what the report says. Yet RadQA results are reported as a single F1 that merges both. We propose an evaluation method that separates them, reporting false-answer and over-abstention rates beside F1 and splitting F1 changes into extraction and answerability terms. We apply it to 13 LLMs on the RadQA test set, zero-shot and with three cumulative demonstration sets, the last adding an unanswerable example. Models with similar F1 differed more than twofold in false-answer rate. The unanswerable example changed when models answered, not how well they extracted: 12 of 13 models abstained more often, and three-quarters of the answers they withdrew had F1 $\geq$ 0.5. Within models, false answers showed no clear association with extraction quality, but acting on the decision itself helped: keeping an answer only when enough other models also answered lowered the zero-shot false-answer rate by 4 points without a detectable F1 change. Because the two decisions can change independently, we suggest radiology QA evaluations report them separately, not through F1 alone.

Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. However, using these models for every step of a long-horizon trajectory incurs substantial inference cost, even though not all steps may require the same level of model capability. In this paper, we find that allocating the LLM to only a small subset of key steps can achieve performance comparable to full LLM execution while significantly reducing inference cost. Motivated by this observation, we propose EdgeWise, an edge-cloud collaboration framework that deploys an SLM on the local device as the primary solver and selectively delegates critical steps to a cloud LLM when stronger model capacity is needed. To enable autonomous delegation without additional models at inference time, we introduce a step-level RL method that jointly optimizes task solving and delegation, with fine-grained credit assignment for individual delegation decisions. We also introduce an external judge-based delegation strategy and use it to systematically investigate key design choices in edge-cloud collaboration, including when to delegate, how delegation decisions should be made, what context should be shared, and how frequently the cloud LLM should be invoked. Experiments show that EdgeWise matches or outperforms pure-LLM execution while reducing inference cost up to 62% on SWE-Rebench and 34% on Terminal-Bench 2.1. We further deploy EdgeWise on a local workstation, demonstrating comparable cost savings in a practical edge-cloud setting.

Compositional RL: Evaluating and Training LLMs for Collaborative Reasoning
组合式强化学习：评估与训练LLM用于协作推理
Language models are often evaluated alone but increasingly deployed together, routed between, made to debate, ensembled, or collaboratively trained. For a model inside a system, what matters most is not how well it performs on its own, but how much the system gains from its presence. We call this a model's compositional strength and formalize it using the Shapley value of a cooperative game over coalitions of a model pool, and use a model's leave-one-out contribution to the full coalition as a tractable proxy, requiring n+1 rather than 2^n system evaluations. Evaluating individual vs. compositional strengths across five model pools, twelve collaboration methods, and twelve datasets, we find them largely uncorrelated: in 12 of 15 (pool, method-family) settings, individual strength does not translate into compositional advantages, and the coupling is weakest among general-purpose models that practitioners are most likely to deploy. Standalone benchmarks are therefore often poor proxies for models' value in collaborative systems. We then propose compositional reinforcement learning (C-RL), which trains a policy inside a live multi-model system and rewards the outcome produced by the system as a whole, rather than the policy's correctness in isolation. The leave-one-out baseline in Shapley values cancels under a group policy gradient, so this needs no additional rollout cost beyond RL on the collaborative system's outcome and never requires running a coalition without the policy. Across three collaboration protocols and eight tasks spanning reasoning, coding, and scientific discovery, C-RL produces the strongest collaborator in 21 of 24 settings, lifting collaborative performance by +4.0 to +5.4 pts on average (~3x the gain of baselines), up to +13.1 pts.

Evaluating Temporal Reasoning in Large Language Models: Event Temporal Relation Extraction with Allen's Interval Algebra, Logical Consistency, and Relative Time in Narratives
评估大语言模型中的时间推理：基于Allen区间代数、逻辑一致性与叙事中相对时间的事件时间关系抽取
Understanding a narrative means knowing how every event relates in time to every other, yet large language models (LLMs) are mostly tested on isolated event pairs or coarse labels. We ask five LLMs to reconstruct the complete network of Allen's 13 interval relations for 360 English narratives whose events are placed relative to one another rather than by dates, and evaluate the outputs under a pre-registered protocol for agreement with our gold annotations, converse consistency and logical satisfiability. End to end, the best model clearly beats trivial baselines on macro-F1, our primary metric, yet under our pre-registered parser no model matches the accuracy of always answering "before", which the skewed labels inflate. Most of that accuracy gap is a parsing artifact: formatting errors in large matrices cost whole rows, and a post hoc parser that recovers the determined cells of malformed rows raises coverage from 0.60 to 0.84 and closes the gap to the baseline for the best model. On the cells they do answer, models recover precedence and containment but rarely overlap, and they fail most on flashbacks, where both the narration and the event list present the later event first. Logical consistency varies widely yet says little about agreement with gold: enforcing it raises accuracy mainly by filling empty cells, and is beaten there by the trivial control of guessing the majority label. Reliable structured output and robust handling of relative time are prerequisites for temporal reasoning over whole narratives.

claimcheck: Measuring and Improving Specification Faithfulness
claimcheck：测量与改进规范忠实性
Formal verification proves that a program satisfies its specification, but says nothing about whether the specification captures what the author meant. As LLMs increasingly write both code and specifications, a gap between the author's natural-language requirement and the specification becomes a live risk. A machine-checked proof of a property narrower than the one requested is worthless but passes every check. Closing this gap is solving the spec formalization problem: given a natural-language requirement, produce a formal artifact whose meaning matches it. To measure the gap, we curate an end-to-end benchmark for spec formalization spanning four formal languages: Dafny contracts and Lean 4, Isabelle and Rocq theorem statements. Each of its 3,234 rows pairs a natural-language requirement with a formal artifact and a label established by execution, by proof, or by the benchmark it is drawn from. A third of the rows are meaning-preserving rewrites of the artifact that keep the faithful label, so a judge cannot score by detecting that a row was edited. We introduce claimcheck, a tool that detects incorrect formalizations: the formal artifact is translated back into plain English by a model that never sees the requirement, and a separate model, the judge, decides whether the informalization and the requirement express the same guarantee. On all four languages it gains 8.2 to 9.8 points of macro recall over a single call shown the requirement and the artifact, and 4.2 to 6.0 over that call handed the same list of meaning-preserving rewrites. Showing the judge the artifact as well costs 1.4 to 4.5 points. Across four judges that also see the artifact, the gain shrinks as the judge gets stronger, to within a point of the informed single call for the strongest.
中文翻译
形式化验证可证明程序满足其规范，但无法说明该规范是否捕捉了作者的真实意图。随着大语言模型越来越多地同时编写代码与规范，作者的自然语言需求与规范之间出现偏差的风险日益凸显。一个比请求范围更窄的属性的机器可检查证明毫无价值，却仍可通过所有检查。弥合这一差距即为解决规范形式化问题：给定自然语言需求，生成一个语义与其匹配的形式化成果。为衡量这一差距，我们构建了一个端到端的规范形式化基准，涵盖四种形式语言：Dafny契约、Lean 4、Isabelle和Rocq定理陈述。该基准共包含3,234行，每行配对一个自然语言需求、一个形式化成果以及由执行、证明或基准本身确立的标签。三分之一的行是保持忠实标签的意义保留重写，因此评判者无法通过检测修改来评分。我们引入claimcheck工具，用于检测错误的形式化：将形式化成果通过一个从未见过需求的模型翻译回自然英语，再由另一个独立模型（裁判）判断该非形式化表达与原始需求是否传达相同保证。在所有四种语言上，claimcheck在单次调用中相比仅展示需求与成果的基准提升8.2至9.8点宏召回率，相比展示相同意义保留重写的基准提升4.2至6.0点。向裁判同时展示成果会损失1.4至4.5点。在四位也看到成果的裁判中，随着裁判能力增强，增益缩小，最强裁判接近于知情单次调用的结果。

The Curse of Knowledge in Role-Playing Language Models
角色扮演语言模型中的知识诅咒
Role-playing language models speak as characters in games and agent simulations, where the system records what each character can hear, see and understand. We test whether characters respect these boundaries in 480 scenes, each with a counterfactual twin that changes only the hidden fact, so mentions of the twin's fact measure guessing. Across 11 open-weight models, characters use content from speech they cannot understand or hear at 67 and 72 percentage points (pp) above this baseline, although most models correctly state what the character perceives. This is a curse of knowledge. The leak extends to hidden actions and private messages and changes where characters search. Five of six proprietary models rarely leak, but compliance in strong models depends on input format. Changing only the scene layout or character description raises the rate in two otherwise compliant open-weight models from under 10 to over 60 pp, and combined changes raise two proprietary models from near zero to 13 and 21~pp. Writing the line as the scene's author leaks nearly as much as role-play, and thinking rarely helps. Giving models only what the character observes stops the leak without hiding what it may report.

Automatic speech recognition (ASR) remains challenging for low-resource languages, where the scarcity of transcribed speech limits the development of accurate systems. This challenge is particularly acute for African languages such as Ewe, which has millions of speakers but remains underrepresented in publicly available ASR resources and benchmarks. In this work, we consolidate, normalize, and partition existing Ewe speech resources into a standardized 174-hour Ewe ASR benchmark, the largest to date to our knowledge. We fine-tune and evaluate pretrained speech models, including Whisper and AfriHuBERT, to establish strong baselines on our benchmark. Welcome to the Age of Agent Ads: Using On-Policy Attacks to Steer Agentic Decisions
智能体广告时代来临：利用在线策略攻击引导智能体决策
People increasingly delegate option-ranking tasks (e.g., shopping, job search, travel) to AI agents, which creates incentives to steer agentic decisions via "agent ads." To defend against such steering attacks, people count on models' alignment training and platforms' terms of service, and consequently the most effective existing attacks are designed to trigger off-policy behaviors. Exposing a new attack surface, we introduce on-policy attacks, which steer agentic decisions without pushing individually aligned behaviors off policy. Our example attack consists of two steps: To remain compliant with platforms' terms of service, we first inject a truthful negation about a fictitious concept ("Does not contain blizyester") into a product description. This triggers an agent to search the web ("What is blizyester?"), which surfaces planted websites full of fabricated information associating the fictitious concept with harmful implications ("Blizyester linked to dementia"). Trained to keep users safe from harm, the agent penalizes every option missing the truthful negation. Evaluating our attack across four real-world listing datasets, we find some frontier models exposed, enabling an adversarial actor to penalize competitors without violating existing platform-listing guidelines. We discuss the broader challenge of regulating advertising aimed at AI agents and provide recommendations to model developers and platform providers.
中文翻译
人们越来越多地将选项排序任务（如购物、求职、旅行）委托给AI智能体，这催生了通过“智能体广告”来引导智能体决策的动机。为防御此类引导攻击，人们依赖模型对齐训练和平台的服务条款，因此现有最有效的攻击均旨在触发离线策略行为。我们揭示了一个新的攻击面，提出在线策略攻击，该攻击在不使个体对齐行为偏离策略的前提下引导智能体决策。我们的示例攻击包含两个步骤：为遵守平台服务条款，首先在产品描述中注入关于虚构概念（“不包含blizyester”）的真值否定；这会触发智能体进行网络搜索（“blizyester是什么？”），从而暴露大量伪造信息网站，将该虚构概念与有害含义关联起来（“blizyester与痴呆相关”）。由于智能体被训练为保护用户免受伤害，因此会惩罚所有缺少该真值否定的选项。我们在四个真实世界列表数据集上评估该攻击，发现部分前沿模型存在漏洞，使得攻击者可在不违反现有平台列表指南的情况下惩罚竞争对手。我们讨论了针对AI智能体广告监管的更广泛挑战，并向模型开发者和平台提供改进建议。

DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
DuoDiscover：突破评估瓶颈的自主发现规模化
Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. A lightweight orchestrator spawns and terminates agents, briefs running ones, and seeds new agents with others' confirmed work. DuoDiscover enables autonomous optimization from software to chip architecture. We demonstrate DuoDiscover on two repository-level benchmarks and four GPU and TPU kernel suites covering hundreds of kernels. On SWE-fficiency, it doubles the average speedup of human experts. On SOL-Exec, it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels and in the top three on 212. On the heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite engines, DuoDiscover achieves 1.92$\times$ and 1.38$\times$ gains over the base code. On a CPU microarchitecture optimization task with evaluations of up to 28 hours, DuoDiscover surpasses both AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, with 1.65$\times$ ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days, advancing the frontier of autonomous chip design.

评估是AI进步的核心，同样对自主发现至关重要。然而，将自主发现扩展至真实工程挑战面临根本性瓶颈：评估进展的成本过高。在实际环境中，一次完整评估（如全基准测试或服务追踪）可能耗时数小时，因此搜索过程只能承担少量真实评估。我们提出DuoDiscover，一个通过三种机制联合高效发现优化目标与评估方式的搜索系统。首先，编码智能体集群中的每个工作节点共同发现一个优化目标和一个快速、定制化的代理评估器（称为标尺），随后智能体在标尺上进行梯度上升而非真实评估。其次，由于搜索可利用标尺与真实目标之间的差距，持续的保真度测试不断验证标尺排名，淘汰任何发生漂移的标尺。第三，该集群采用自下而上的结构，无中央问题分解。轻量级协调器负责启动、终止智能体，简要通知运行中的智能体，并以其他已确认的工作为种子生成新智能体。DuoDiscover实现了从软件到芯片架构的自主优化。我们在两个仓库级基准和四个GPU/TPU内核套件（涵盖数百个内核）上进行了演示。在SWE-fficiency上，其平均加速效果是人类专家的两倍；在SOL-Exec上，它在235个内核中排名第一121次，在前三位中占212次。在高度优化的vLLM和SQLite引擎上，DuoDiscover分别实现1.92×和1.38×的性能提升。在一项CPU微架构优化任务中，评估耗时长达28小时，DuoDiscover在16.7天内超越基于AlphaEvolve的ArchAgent v2和最佳人类设计，实现1.65×的性能增益，推动了自主芯片设计的前沿。

AD4EDU: Benchmarking University Lecture Audio Description across Accessibility Standards, Metrics, and Learner Preferences
AD4EDU：跨无障碍标准、评估指标与学习者偏好的大学讲座音频描述基准测试
Audio description (AD) aims to enhance the accessibility of visual media for blind and low-vision (BLV) persons. However, in higher education, where slide-based lectures are a default mode of teaching, lecture AD remains largely underexplored. The main reason is that existing production guidelines, evaluation metrics, and benchmark datasets are oriented toward entertainment content and do not transfer to lectures, where ADs must complement the lecturer's speech, resolve deictic references, and fit within narrow pauses. In this work, we propose AD4Edu, consisting of an AD benchmark, AD4Edu-Bench, and a rule-diagnosable evaluation metric, AD4Edu-Eval, for generating and evaluating ADs in higher education. Specifically, we consolidated established accessibility guidance, including WCAG 2.2, the DCMP Description Key, and NCAM's STEM description practices. We further collected silver reference ADs, judge-ordered preference pairs, and pairwise preferences from four BLV raters, and post-trained models with direct preference optimization (DPO) for detailed analysis. Our findings indicate that while the metric reliably detects violations of the standard, ADs that comply with it do not necessarily fulfill the subjective preferences of BLV persons, most notably on description length, underscoring the necessity of active participation of BLV persons in co-designing inclusive AI solutions.

MENTOR: Procedural Shielding of Tool-Using LLM Agents
MENTOR：面向使用工具的LLM智能体的程序化防护
Tool-using LLM agents are increasingly used to automate workflows governed by procedural manuals, such as company rules for booking travel or procuring hardware. These manuals are written in natural language for humans and describe general requirements over such complex workflows. Ensuring compliance of LLM agents with these manuals is difficult, and state-of-the-art techniques use either LLM judges or manually written rules to forbid problematic tool-calls locally at runtime. This is insufficient because (i) only blocking tool calls keeps the agent clueless about how to make correct progress towards fulfilling its task, and (ii) can lead to overly conservative behavior of the agent, as tool calls might only be problematic in certain contexts. To overcome these challenges, we introduce MENTOR, which (i) additionally provides guidance for the agent to make procedural-compliant progress on the task, and (ii) ensures that this compliance is context-aware. We achieve these goals by building a novel history-dependent runtime shield that is obtained from the procedural manual via a multi-step autoformalization pipeline. At its core, MENTOR utilizes a game-based technique to ensure robustness against runtime uncertainty without over-resticting agents' behavior. This yields a formally assisted framework for procedural shielding of LLM agents that improves compliance well beyond existing methods. In particular, MENTOR lifts the compliance of shielded light-weight open-source LLMs above that of non-shielded proprietary models. Since a shield is synthesized once per manual and then serves every task, a MENTOR-shielded agent becomes a viable choice for repeatedly executed workflows, potentially reducing deployment costs when the offline construction cost is amortized over repeated tasks.

Lexical Redefinition Reveals Context-Sensitive Instruction Following
词汇重定义揭示上下文敏感的指令遵循
How do language models reconcile conflicting contextual evidence within a prompt? We study this question using lexical redefinition, where an explicit instruction specifies how a word should be interpreted and a subsequent sentence provides additional evidence through its usage. Across 870 word pairs, we find that lexical redefinitions are not applied as fixed rules. Instead, the behaviour depends systematically on the relationship between the explicit instruction and the intervening sentence: the contextualised usage can preserve, weaken, or completely reverse the instruction. These results suggest that the interpretation of an explicit instruction remains sensitive to subsequent contextual evidence. Lexical redefinition therefore provides a controlled behavioural paradigm for studying how language models integrate multiple sources of information within a prompt.

SpecGuardBench: Can Coding Agents Construct Reliable Validation Harnesses from Natural Language Specifications?
SpecGuardBench：编码智能体能否从自然语言规范中构建可靠的验证测试套件？
As coding agents become more capable, tests remain the primary evidence for judging whether their code is correct. Yet passing available tests does not establish that an implementation satisfies its natural language specification. Reliable validation requires checks that faithfully capture the specification and scenarios that thoroughly exercise the code, but current benchmarks provide limited insight into whether agents can construct such evidence themselves. We introduce SpecGuardBench, a benchmark of 291 tasks from 13 real-world repositories, covering 8 types of verification logic such as functional postconditions and interaction protocols. Given a natural language specification, repository context, and a reference implementation, an agent constructs a validation harness comprising executable checks and test scenarios. The checks should reject implementations that violate the specification while accepting those that satisfy it, and the scenarios should thoroughly exercise the code. Across four proprietary and open-weight coding agents, none constructs a harness scored as faithful on the benchmark's implementations for more than 63% of the tasks. The bottleneck lies less in exploring test scenarios than in constructing checks that faithfully reflect the specification. Specifically, the agents show a clear tendency to write checks that mirror the reference implementation rather than the specification, and therefore reject implementations that the specification permits.

ANCHOR: Assessing Naturalistic Constraint Hierarchies and Ordering in Repository-Grounded Agentic Coding
ANCHOR：评估基于仓库的代理编码中的自然约束层次与排序
For repository-grounded coding agents, a functionally correct patch is not necessarily an acceptable one: developers also constrain how the task must be carried out-modification scope, workflow order, validation, tool use, and reporting. This capability, which we call engineering constraint following, remains largely invisible to current evaluations. We introduce ANCHOR (Assessing Naturalistic Constraint Hierarchies and Ordering in Repository-Grounded Agentic Coding), a benchmark built on naturalistic, multilingual repository tasks spanning eight language groups. ANCHOR combines (i) a hierarchical taxonomy of 10 categories and 78 leaf types distilled from real developer interactions, (ii) an automated pipeline that instantiates task-grounded atomic constraints and composes them into typed AND/THEN/PRIORITY relations, and (iii) a trajectory-grounded evaluation framework that checks both the code diff and the execution trajectory with rule-based and LLM judges. Across 19 agent configurations spanning 2 scaffolds and 10 foundation models on 358 tasks, the strongest measured system, Claude Opus 4.8 under Cline, reaches 70.1% atomic compliance and 63.7% relation compliance, while 19.0% of tasks pass every scored checklist item under the strict all-item FCCR criterion. A five-engineer audit of constraints from 50 instances reports 94% feasibility, 94% repository consistency, and 96% realism. In the primary paired set (14 configurations), the mean signed change in task completion after adding constraints is +0.7 percentage points; individual changes vary in both directions. These results distinguish functional success from constraint compliance, with failures concentrated in workflow ordering, tool-use discipline, and reporting, and substantial interactions between models and scaffolds.

对于基于仓库的编码智能体而言，功能正确的补丁未必是可接受的：开发者还对任务的执行方式施加约束——修改范围、工作流顺序、验证、工具使用和报告等。我们将这种能力称为工程约束遵循，但目前的评估体系对此几乎毫无察觉。我们提出ANCHOR（评估基于仓库的代理编码中的自然约束层次与排序），一个基于自然、多语言仓库任务的基准，涵盖八个语言群体。ANCHOR结合了三方面内容：(i) 从真实开发者互动中提炼出的10个类别和78个叶节点类型的层次化分类体系；(ii) 自动化流水线，将任务相关的原子约束实例化并组合成带类型的关系（AND/THEN/PRIORITY）；(iii) 基于轨迹的评估框架，使用基于规则和LLM的裁判检查代码差异和执行轨迹。在358个任务上，对19种智能体配置（跨越2种架构和10个基础模型）的评估显示，最强系统（Claude Opus 4.8在Cline下）达到70.1%的原子合规率和63.7%的关系合规率，而在严格全项FCCR标准下，仅有19.0%的任务通过所有评分检查项。五名工程师对50个实例的审计结果显示，约束的可行性、仓库一致性和现实性分别达94%、94%和96%。在主配对集（14种配置）中，加入约束后的任务完成率平均变化为+0.7个百分点；个体变化方向各异。这些结果区分了功能成功与约束合规，失败集中于工作流排序、工具使用纪律和报告环节，且模型与架构之间存在显著交互作用。

Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
对比中的迷失：用于可靠视觉问答的指令保持解码
Visual contrastive decoding corrects answers using the prediction difference between the original image and a reference condition, yet the same contrast also turns supported abstentions into incorrect answers. We find that abstentions are lost at two stages: contrastive decoding with candidate filtering can exclude the abstention token before any comparison takes place, and the reference branch's response to the abstention instruction is removed when the reference prediction is subtracted. We therefore propose instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the effect of the abstention instruction on the original-image prediction intact while leaving the contrast strength freely adjustable. Using a perturbed image and an image-free prediction as references, we obtain IP-VCD and IP-M3ID. On decision utility (DU), which credits both correct answers and supported abstentions, both methods outperform all compared non-IP baselines on every one of nine models on VizWiz, and IP-VCD also leads on eight of nine models on Food-101. Candidate measurements and paired per-question comparisons show that computing the instruction effect and the visual contrast term separately lets contrastive decoding support both correct answers and supported abstentions.

Teacher rationales can help a smaller model answer health professions questions, but they can also reinforce errors. We examined when they help and how this evidence can guide training using Brazilian Portuguese questions from medical and multiprofessional residency examinations. First, we measured how a teacher rationale changed the student's probability of selecting the correct answer and compared this effect with rationales drawn from other questions. The complete rationale increased this probability by 21~p.p. when the teacher was correct and decreased it by 14~p.p. when the teacher was wrong. By intervening on the reasoning content, we showed that shuffled rationales did not produce the same pattern. Guided by this result, we trained only with rationales attached to correct teacher answers and compared answer-only training, step-by-step distillation, and our proposed Distill-SFT method. Distill-SFT showed a modest advantage over step-by-step distillation on previously missed questions under reasoning, while using fewer training instances by combining the answer and rationale into a single target. We also investigated catastrophic forgetting using the out-of-domain ENEM dataset. Answer-only training reduced reasoning accuracy by 12~p.p. relative to baseline, compared with approximately 4~p.p. for either rationale-based training method. Together, these findings support a workflow that audits rationale content before distillation, verifies teacher answers before supervision, and trains compact models efficiently for health professions question answering.

EHR-Bench: A Chinese Multi-Task Benchmark for Recruitment AI

Recruitment applications span diverse operations, from drafting job descriptions and interpreting queries to organizing profiles, assessing fit, and recommending candidates and jobs. Systematic LLM evaluation therefore requires task coverage that reflects this range of business needs. We introduce EHR-Bench, an open Chinese benchmark comprising twelve tasks across six capability families and five recruitment scenarios. The tasks cover generation, extraction, classification, retrieval, semantic similarity, and reciprocal ranking within one evaluation framework. An internal recruitment dataset guides task definitions, the occupation taxonomy and sampling targets, output requirements, and scoring protocols. Following these specifications, we construct 8,336 task instances from public materials and controlled augmentation, with source-aware expert review and documented provenance. We evaluate twelve LLMs through task-level, capability-level, and aggregate comparisons. Closely ranked models exhibit distinct task strengths, and performance varies across input sources, reference evidence, and candidate pools. Five shared models retain the same observed Overall ordering on a private operational reference, with variation in capability and task correspondence. EHR-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for systematic model assessment, task-specific model selection, and further research on LLMs for recruitment. The project repository is available at https://github.com/EhrBench/EHR-Bench.

PatTransBench: an ipc-stratified, multi-dimensional benchmark for patent machine translation evaluation

We present PatTransBench, a 12,000-item Chinese-English/Japanese/Korean patent machine translation (PatMT) benchmark with a four-dimensional evaluation protocol. The benchmark comprises 6,000 short-text (sentence/claim) and 6,000 long-text (paragraph) pairs, evenly split across three language pairs and both translation directions, built via IPC-section-stratified sampling and dualthreshold quality gating from upstream patent-family parallel corpora. The evaluation protocol spans literal n-gram overlap (BLEU, ROUGE-L, chrF), cross-lingual semantic textual similarity (CLSTS), 38-probe-language consistency testing, and serving performance under concurrency. A case study on PatMT2-7B and its fp8/AWQ4/AutoRound-4bit variants reveals direction-dependent quantization effects masked by aggregate scores and non-monotonic language-failure patterns across quantization schemes that are invisible to single-metric evaluation. We plan to release the benchmark, protocol, and case-study results upon publication to support reproducible PatMT evaluation.

The growing use of language models for forecasting motivates a broader evaluation of their world-model capabilities. Such evaluation must go beyond predictive accuracy to assess hidden-state inference and intervention prediction. Real-world forecasting benchmarks offer limited access to hidden-state ground truth and controlled experiments. We introduce CivWorldBench, a benchmark built on a multi-agent strategy game engine with recorded internal states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts. Its 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds support three task levels: association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction. Reference predictors support attributable evaluation of capability gaps, with an expert harness and empirical ceiling estimates contextualizing scores. Stored trajectories make intermediate predictions verifiable, while agent-play experiments test whether world-model capabilities support decision-making. The main panel comprises eleven frontier language models. Composite benchmark scores correlate with real-world forecasting leaderboards on matched model panels, more closely than with a general-capability index, supporting its use as a proxy for real-world forecasting capability. Strong association forecasts do not consistently extend to belief inference or intervention prediction, and effect magnitudes remain poorly calibrated despite informative direction predictions. Process verification reveals errors missed by final-answer evaluation, and structured reasoning improves intervention prediction for the strongest model in the process study. Agent-play experiments identify useful assisted plans and motivate evaluating decision-relevant capabilities beyond association forecasting. These findings identify hidden-state inference, intermediate-state prediction, and effect calibration as priorities for world-model training.

语言模型在预测任务中的日益广泛应用，推动了对其世界模型能力的更广泛评估。此类评估必须超越预测准确性，以评估隐藏状态推断和干预预测能力。现实世界预测基准对隐藏状态真实值的访问有限，且缺乏受控实验条件。我们引入CivWorldBench，一个基于多智能体策略游戏引擎构建的基准测试，包含记录的内部状态、受控观测和配对干预回放。其来自475个世界的1,900个决策点支持三个任务层级：关联预测、信念推断和干预预测。参考预测器支持能力差距的可归因评估，专家引导和经验上限估计有助于理解得分上下文。存储轨迹使中间预测可验证，而智能体对战实验检验世界模型能力是否支持决策制定。主面板包含十一款前沿语言模型。综合基准得分与真实世界预测排行榜在匹配模型组上的相关性高于通用能力指数，支持其作为真实世界预测能力的代理指标。强关联预测并未一致延伸至信念推断或干预预测，尽管方向预测具信息量，但效应幅度仍校准不足。过程验证揭示了最终答案评估所遗漏的错误，结构化推理提升了最强模型在过程研究中的干预预测表现。智能体对战实验识别出有用的辅助计划，促使我们超越关联预测，评估决策相关的其他能力。这些发现指出隐藏状态推断、中间状态预测和效应校准是世界模型训练的优先方向。

RIFT: Token Influence Follows the Path of Least Resistance
RIFT：标记影响遵循阻力最小路径
Which context tokens drive a language model's answer? Graph-based tools such as attention rollout and attention flow answer this from a single forward pass, yet their faithfulness in decoder-only models is rarely tested against interventions. We view the layers of a decoder as a causal network whose conductances are attention weights, and read a token's influence on the answer from the resistance between them. We propose RIFT (Resistance-based Information Flow in Transformers), which scores a token by the series resistance of its path of least resistance to the answer, found exactly by a classic shortest-path dynamic program. On synthetic in-context retrieval tasks and extractive question answering over Wikipedia paragraphs, RIFT predicts the effect of replacing a token with a Spearman correlation of 0.52-0.68; predicting a single replacement, it reaches 77-96% of the agreement between two different random replacements. It needs no gradients and no extra forward passes, scoring every token of a prompt in 0.9-3.4 ms on one CPU thread, whereas the replacement experiment needs a forward pass per token. On 576 held-out prompts from four models of two families (Qwen3 and Llama 3.2), it outperforms token distance, attention rollout and attention flow in every pre-specified comparison, by 0.23 to 0.88 in mean Spearman correlation, and it is the best or tied-best of all attention-based scores we test. Aggregates that add up all routes (attention flow, effective resistance and rollout) instead mostly encode token position: as a simple proposition shows, early tokens have many more parallel routes to the answer.

Avoiding What Your Teacher Already Knows: Entity Familiarity for Deep-Search Distillation
避免重复教师已知内容：面向深度搜索蒸馏的实体熟悉度
Deep-search agents are commonly trained by distilling tool-use trajectories from stronger teacher models. However, structurally complex questions may remain relatively easy for teachers familiar with key entities in the underlying entity graph, resulting in lower search demand and weaker supervision. We refer to this teacher-specific variation in question difficulty as teacher-relative difficulty and investigate entity familiarity as an early predictor. We first introduce Evidence-Verified Entity Familiarity (EVF), which estimates familiarity by verifying a teacher-generated factual brief against online evidence. Across multiple teachers, EVF is significantly correlated with teacher-relative difficulty with AUCs of 0.60--0.70. However, its high cost makes it impractical for constructing entity graphs at scale. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Reported Entity Familiarity (SEF), a lightweight gating signal that directly asks a teacher whether it is familiar with an entity before admitting that entity into the graph. Across multiple teachers, trajectories from SEF-gated synthesis exhibit greater observed search demand and yield higher downstream student accuracy than those from ungated synthesis. Because familiarity is teacher specific, we further study cross-teacher reuse. We screen graphs collected for other teachers using Kimi-K3's SEF judgments and use the retained graphs to produce 5,411 additional trajectories. Combined with 2,200 trajectories from newly constructed, SEF-gated graphs, these data improve Qwen3.8-27B's accuracy from 44.10% to 66.41% on a BrowseComp subset, and achieving state-of-the-art performance among models of comparable size on BrowseComp, SEAL-0, HLE-text, and xbench. Overall, SEF provides a low-cost way to synthesize more informative supervision for deep-search distillation.

深度搜索代理通常通过蒸馏更强教师模型的工具使用轨迹进行训练。然而，对于结构复杂的提问，若教师对底层实体图中的关键实体熟悉，则问题相对容易，导致搜索需求较低，监督信号较弱。我们将这种由教师决定的问题难度变化称为教师相对难度，并研究实体熟悉度作为早期预测因子。我们首先引入证据验证的实体熟悉度（EVF），通过验证教师生成的事实摘要与在线证据的一致性来估计熟悉度。在多个教师中，EVF与教师相对难度显著相关，AUC达0.60–0.70。但其高成本使其难以大规模构建实体图。为此，我们提出自报告实体熟悉度（SEF），一种轻量级门控信号，直接询问教师是否熟悉某实体后再决定是否将其纳入图中。在多个教师中，SEF门控合成的轨迹表现出更高的实际搜索需求，并带来更高的下游学生模型准确率。由于熟悉度具有教师特异性，我们进一步研究跨教师复用。我们使用Kimi-K3的SEF判断筛选其他教师收集的图，并保留的图生成了5,411条新轨迹。结合新构建的SEF门控图中的2,200条轨迹，使Qwen3.8-27B在BrowseComp子集上的准确率从44.10%提升至66.41%，在与之规模相当的模型中达到领先水平，覆盖BrowseComp、SEAL-0、HLE-text和xbench等多个基准。总体而言，SEF提供了一种低成本方式，用于为深度搜索蒸馏合成更具信息量的监督信号。
