Active Learning for Finding a Needle in a Haystack
主动学习寻找针尖中的稻草
Training a classifier to find a rare class of documents, such as hate speech directed at a particular religious group, requires labelled examples that are expensive to obtain when the class makes up only a small fraction of a corpus. Active learning reduces this cost, but it must start from an initial labelled set that contains examples of the target class. Random sampling cannot supply these at reasonable cost, so they must be selected in some other way, such as keyword search, and any such selection biases the initial set towards part of the target class. We evaluate whether active learning can correct this bias. On AG News and Measuring Hate Speech, at a prevalence of around 1%, we compare random sampling with eight active learning strategies, starting from initial sets that cover or omit known subgroups of the target class, and measure recall on the omitted subgroups as well as F1. On AG News, almost every strategy recovers the omitted subgroup. On Measuring Hate Speech, uncertainty-based strategies recover less of the omitted subgroups than random sampling, whereas discriminative active learning recovers 55% of them without a significant loss of F1. Aggregate metrics conceal these differences.

训练分类器以识别罕见文档类别（如针对特定宗教群体的仇恨言论）需要标注样本，而当该类别仅占语料库极小比例时，获取这些样本成本高昂。主动学习可降低此成本，但必须从包含目标类别样本的初始标注集开始。随机采样无法以合理成本提供这些样本，因此必须通过其他方式选择，如关键词搜索，但这会使得初始集偏向目标类别的部分子集。我们评估主动学习能否纠正这种偏差。在AG News和Measuring Hate Speech数据集上，当目标类别占比约为1%时，我们比较了随机采样与八种主动学习策略，初始集涵盖或遗漏已知的目标子群，并测量遗漏子群的召回率以及F1分数。在AG News上，几乎所有策略都恢复了遗漏子群；而在Measuring Hate Speech上，基于不确定性的策略比随机采样更难恢复遗漏子群，而判别式主动学习在F1无显著损失的情况下恢复了55%的遗漏子群。总体指标掩盖了这些差异。

A language model's ability to solve a task individually does not ensure that a team can solve it under unequal access to information and communication. SANZARU examines this gap through cooperative bomb-defusal puzzles adapted from BOMBANANA! (Lefto Studio, 2026). Task information and action authority are divided among three agents: one cannot hear, another cannot speak, and the third cannot see. The benchmark contains 120 puzzle instances across seven families, each targeting a distinct coordination ability. Across 1512 episodes, 7 models achieve an overall success rate of 49%, ranging from 20% to 86% under the evaluated configurations. Teams develop or adopt diverse communication protocols, from simple gesture codes to Morse and encodings of entire manuals. Yet trace analysis attributes about 60% of 771 team losses to communication, and agents attempt to use channels unavailable to their teammates despite explicit role instructions. Together, task outcomes and interaction traces enable evaluation of both collaborative performance and perspective taking throughout cooperation. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/markli404/sanzaru-benchmark.

Where Did We Go Wrong? Localizing Errors to Repair Multi-Turn Conversations
我们错在哪里？定位错误以修复多轮对话
Large language model (LLM) assistants are increasingly used in multi-turn conversations, where the user's intent is often unclear at first and revealed only gradually over time. The assistant must therefore interpret each exchange and form inferences about the user's intent, using them to update its working state. These updates usually refine the assistant's understanding, but a misinterpretation can instead corrupt its working state by ruling out the true intent, influencing subsequent turns and ultimately causing the conversation to fail. Efficient recovery then requires locating and revising the misinterpretation without discarding information that remains valid. We introduce Loci (Localization Of Corrupted Inferences), a framework for probabilistically localizing misinterpretations and selectively repairing the assistant's working state. Given an observed failure, Loci reasons over possible user intents and assigns each update a probability of having excluded the true intent. These probabilities rank suspected updates and quantify the model's confidence in the localization of the underlying misinterpretations. Loci then uses this information in a repair policy that decides whether to retain, verify, or remove suspected updates, enabling recovery from corrupted inferences while preserving useful information. To evaluate Loci's ability to identify misinterpretations, we first test it in a controlled setup with injected errors. We find that Loci improves localization over the baselines, with its advantage becoming larger when multiple errors occur. We then evaluate it in free-form conversations, where misinterpretations arise naturally, and measure the interactions needed to complete the task after an initial failure. Using localization confidence to guide repair, Loci reduces mean recovery cost by 46-79% relative to the strongest baseline across multiple domains.

大型语言模型（LLM）助手越来越多地用于多轮对话中，用户的意图通常起初不明确，而是随着时间逐步揭示。因此，助手必须解释每次交流并推断用户意图，用以更新其工作状态。这些更新通常会细化助手的理解，但误判却可能通过排除真实意图而污染其工作状态，进而影响后续对话回合，最终导致对话失败。高效的恢复需要在不丢弃仍有效的信息的前提下，定位并修正误判。我们提出了Loci（被污染推理的定位），一种概率化定位误判并选择性修复助手工作状态的框架。给定一个观察到的失败，Loci在可能的用户意图之间进行推理，并为每次更新分配一个排除真实意图的概率。这些概率对可疑更新进行排序，并量化模型对底层误判定位的信心。随后，Loci利用该信息制定修复策略，决定是否保留、验证或移除可疑更新，从而在保留有用信息的同时实现对被污染推理的恢复。为了评估Loci识别误判的能力，我们首先在注入错误的受控环境中测试它。结果发现，Loci在定位方面优于基线，且当出现多个错误时优势更加明显。接着我们在自由形式对话中评估其表现，其中误判自然发生，并测量初始失败后完成任务所需的交互次数。通过使用定位置信度指导修复，Loci在多个领域内相对于最强基线将平均恢复成本降低了46-79%。

Argument structures represent how individual arguments interact within a discourse. However, leveraging these structures to infer meaningful knowledge remains challenging, as it requires a formal representation of how argumentative influence propagates across the structure. We propose Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning System (NARS) for performing persuasiveness detection directly from online discussions. The neural component employs retrieval-augmented iterative LLM reasoning to extract bipolar argument structures, while the symbolic component applies gradual argumentation semantics to propagate argumentative influence over the structure. Using the Webis-CMV-20 corpus, we construct CMV2BAS, a dataset of long, multi-threaded ChangeMyView discussions annotated with LLM-derived bipolar argument structures and labeled with delta events (view change vs.\ no change). We investigate whether gradual argumentation semantics can effectively detect persuasiveness, whether augmenting them with argument quality and graph-based centrality improves performance, and whether symbolic reasoning remains necessary in the presence of modern LLMs. NARS achieves F1=0.57 and AUC=0.56 under its best configuration, outperforming zero-shot Qwen3.6:27B and GPT-oss:20B. We identify support-dominant discussions and long argumentative chains as key failure modes limiting attack influence propagation. Our work demonstrates the feasibility of operationalizing formal gradual argumentation semantics over noisy real-world discourse for scalable macro-level persuasion analysis, while highlighting key challenges and directions for future research in neuro-symbolic argumentation reasoning. We release both CMV2BAS dataset and the NARS framework for public use.

论证结构表示个体论证在话语中的相互作用方式。然而，利用这些结构推断有意义的知识仍然具有挑战性，因为它需要形式化表达论证影响力如何在结构中传播。我们提出了神经符号论证推理系统（NARS），用于直接从在线讨论中执行说服力检测。神经组件采用检索增强的迭代式大语言模型推理，提取双极论证结构；符号组件则应用渐进式论证语义，在结构上传播论证影响力。我们使用Webis-CMV-20语料库构建CMV2BAS数据集，该数据集包含带有大语言模型生成的双极论证结构标注和delta事件标签（观点改变 vs. 无改变）的长篇多线程ChangeMyView讨论。我们研究了渐进式论证语义是否能有效检测说服力，是否通过引入论证质量与基于图的中心性特征可提升性能，以及在现代大语言模型存在的情况下，符号推理是否仍有必要。NARS在最佳配置下达到F1=0.57和AUC=0.56，优于零样本Qwen3.6:27B和GPT-oss:20B。我们识别出支持主导型讨论和长论证链是限制攻击影响力传播的关键失败模式。本工作展示了在嘈杂的真实世界话语上操作形式化渐进式论证语义以实现可扩展的宏观层面说服力分析的可行性，同时指出了神经符号论证推理未来研究的关键挑战与方向。我们已公开发布CMV2BAS数据集和NARS框架。

Automated disease classification from patient-reported symptoms requires balancing the speed of lightweight discriminative models against the contextual understanding and latency costs of autoregressive large language models (LLMs). Decision foundation models offer an alternative by mapping representations directly to candidate classes without free-form text generation. We adapt Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark. Using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) with differential learning rates and a stratified split of 960 training and 240 test cases, the model achieves 95.42% diagnostic accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.9551. This improves upon the reported zero-shot baselines of 61.67% for a remote API and 65.00% for a local unadapted initialization, and outperforms the ClinicalBERT baseline (90.90%). By evaluating candidate logits in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding, inference takes under 80 milliseconds per record on a single GPU, yielding a reported 31-fold speedup over generative LLM baselines. To examine symptom-level evidence, we introduce a Leave-One-Symptom-Out (LOSO) counterfactual perturbation framework. Removing disease-defining symptom clauses in a psoriasis example reduces predicted-class confidence from 100.00% to 0.12% and shifts the prediction to impetigo with 99.59% confidence, while removing secondary systemic symptoms produces less than 0.01% change in confidence. These findings suggest that decision-based architectures can combine the linguistic capabilities of large foundation models with low-latency inference and symptom-level interpretability for clinical triage.

Do Personalized LLMs Need the Whole Conversation? Matching the Full History with Only 5% of Its Text via Relevance-Filtered Context

Personalized assistants accumulate long conversation histories, and passing the whole history to an LLM with every request is costly. We show that it is also unnecessary. On PersonaMem-v2 (180 questions), with GPT-5.6-terra and Claude Opus 5.5 as judges, a relevance-filtered context, built by sentence-level retrieval that ranks the history by similarity to the current request and stops at a fixed budget, matches full-history accuracy with only 5% of the text, cutting the judge's input about 20-fold. An LLM summary of the same length performs on par, but it needs an LLM to read the entire history, whereas retrieval needs only a small embedding model. While both sentence-level retrieval and LLM summary perform strongly, retrieval does so while placing the relevant evidence in the context for only 61% of the questions, and an oracle given only that evidence beats the full history by 15.6 points, making better context selection a promising path to surpassing the full history.

FidelityQ: Preserving Predictive Fidelity in Ultra-Low-Bit Language Model Quantization
FidelityQ：在超低比特语言模型量化中保持预测保真度
Ultra-low-bit scalar quantization offers a regular arithmetic structure for efficient deployment of large language models, but preserving predictive behavior at extreme precision remains challenging: with only a few reconstruction levels, accurate weight representation must translate into consistent predictions from a small calibration set. We propose FidelityQ, a scalar quantization framework that preserves predictive fidelity at weight precisions down to 2 bits. For accurate quantization, we introduce Information-Aligned Analytic Coding (IAC), which shapes each weight row toward a centered symmetric source via randomized Hadamard mixing and fits a mirrored four-level minimum-distortion quantizer to its empirical weights. Every level set in this family decomposes exactly into two sign-valued bases with associated scales, combining source-adaptive reconstruction with lookup-free decoding compatible with scaled integer arithmetic. Our analysis further shows that residual predictive discrepancies are heavy-tailed and concentrate on tokens the teacher predicts confidently, motivating Knowledge-Intensive Calibration (KIC) for consistent quantization. KIC ranks sequences by the tail of token-wise teacher-student divergence, allocates a limited calibration budget to the highest-scoring samples, and restores predictive agreement by updating only quantization levels and scales under teacher supervision, keeping pretrained weights frozen. Experiments on the LLaMA and Qwen families demonstrate the effectiveness of FidelityQ in weight-only and joint quantization settings. On LLaMA-2-7B, FidelityQ achieves a WikiText2 perplexity of 6.62 at W2A16 and improves the prior state-of-the-art W2A4KV4 result from 8.31 to 6.96, while reducing linear-layer weight memory by 8.0x relative to FP16.
中文翻译
超低比特标量量化为大规模语言模型的高效部署提供了规则的算术结构，但在极端精度下保持预测行为仍具挑战性：仅有少数重建级别时，准确的权重表示必须转化为小校准集上的一致预测。我们提出FidelityQ，一种标量量化框架，可在权重精度低至2比特时保持预测保真度。为实现精确量化，我们引入信息对齐分析编码（IAC），通过随机哈达玛混合将每行权重塑造成中心对称源，并为其经验权重拟合一个镜像四层最小失真量化器。该家族中的每一层级可精确分解为两个带相关缩放因子的符号基，结合源自适应重建与无需查表的解码，兼容缩放整数运算。我们的分析进一步表明，残差预测差异呈重尾分布，集中在教师模型自信预测的标记上，由此提出知识密集型校准（KIC）以实现一致量化。KIC根据标记级教师-学生差异尾部对序列排序，将有限校准预算分配给得分最高的样本，并在教师监督下仅更新量化级别和缩放因子，保持预训练权重不变。在LLaMA和Qwen系列上的实验表明，FidelityQ在仅权重量化和联合量化设置下均有效。在LLaMA-2-7B上，FidelityQ在W2A16下达到WikiText2困惑度6.62，并将先前最优结果W2A4KV4的8.31提升至6.96，同时相比FP16将线性层权重内存减少8.0倍。

Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction (ECPE) requires identifying the causes associated with emotions expressed in a conversation. Accurate extraction can depend on evidence that is not initially available, making it important to decide when further information is worth acquiring. We study agent-guided evidence acquisition for ECPE, where a student agent selectively accesses expert judgments for borderline relations on both sides of its validation-selected F1 decision boundary and revises only queried predictions. Through controlled comparisons under different information-access conditions, we examine how delegation granularity, query selection, and response integration affect prediction quality. At a nominal 10% query rate, selective fusion improves mean pair F1 by 2.64-3.88 points over the student in our main experiments, reaching 65.14 on ECF and 49.74 on MEC4 across model families. Our analysis suggests that greater access does not always translate into better cause identification. These findings motivate acquisition strategies that consider both the relevance of newly available evidence and its effect on prediction revision, providing an empirical basis for more effective and efficient evidence acquisition in ECPE.

Aspect Sentiment Quadruple Prediction (ASQP) is fundamentally a relational reasoning problem: identifying aspect-opinion-category-sentiment quadruples requires modeling structured dependencies, not merely sequential co-occurrence. Existing LLM-based approaches incorporate syntactic information indirectly, via retrieval-based demonstration selection or multi-stage training, rather than as unified, single-pass generation-time context. We present DRIFT, which linearizes dependency parse trees and injects them directly into LLM prompts as explicit relational context, enabling the model to reason over aspect-opinion dependencies rather than infer them from token proximity alone. DRIFT further integrates retrieval-augmented in-context learning and a syntax-aware LLM-based adjudication mechanism that complements exact-match evaluation under span-boundary variation. On SemEval Rest15, Rest16, and ACOS, DRIFT achieves the strongest performance among compared generative ASQP methods, reaching 54.47% and 64.10% F1 on Rest15 and Rest16, with consistent gains across short- and medium-distance aspect-opinion configurations; adjudication further shows exact-match metrics systematically underestimate semantically correct predictions.

Biomedical Named Entity Linking (BioNEL) is the task of mapping mentions extracted from biomedical texts to canonical entities or concepts in the standardized knowledge base. Although existing methods have achieved remarkable performance in mapping accuracy, most rely on training with domain-specific datasets, which fundamentally limits their cross-domain adaptability. To address this limitation, we propose BioNEL-RAG, a novel training-free framework that combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with large language models (LLMs). Within this framework, the RAG module focuses on retrieving candidate entities, while the large language model module plays the role of selecting the most appropriate candidate for entity normalization, which is based on the analysis of the mention's context, with the aid of its remarkable text comprehension capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that BioNEL-RAG achieves performance comparable to existing methods without requiring training on subdomain datasets, whereas these methods necessitate fine-tuning on specific subdomains such as genes, diseases, or chemical compounds.

The system integrates a statistical machine translation (SMT) component for query translation, a maximum-entropy named entity recognition (NER) component for Amharic text processing, semantic-based indexing, question analysis, passage retrieval, and answer extraction. For Amharic-to-English retrieval, the system achieved 72% precision and 79% recall; for English-to-Amharic retrieval, it achieved 65% precision and 70% recall. These findings show that a modular translation-and-retrieval architecture can provide useful cross-language access even under low-resource conditions. This revised article preserves the original experimental claims while situating them in the context of subsequent multilingual transformer and Amharic QA research.

Large language models are increasingly deployed in applications that act on users' long-term behavior histories, from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising systems. These applications demand the user dimension of LLM intelligence: inferring a person's preferences, intent, and likely future actions from weeks to years of behavior data. Yet current models are trained on static text or synthetic data, neither of which captures how user behavior evolves over time. Real-world behavior records, already available at scale on content platforms and in personal-assistant agents, offer a natural supervisory signal. From the anonymized behavior records of 100,000 users, Vela generates 100,000 tasks across 91 real-world task templates; difficulty-based filtering and trajectory acceptance criteria retain approximately 75,000 tasks with selected training trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories improves performance over the base model by up to 11.5 points on user-related tasks and by an average of 4 points on general benchmarks. Training on more user behavior data further improves user-related performance, and reinforcement learning after fine-tuning outperforms reinforcement learning from the base model by up to 7.7 points. These gains suggest that real-world user behavior is a scalable source of supervision for both user-centered capabilities and the broader intelligence of LLMs.

Large language models have advanced medical reasoning, but clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains challenging because prescription decisions require integrating domain knowledge, syndrome differentiation, treatment principles, herbal prescription composition, and dosage determination. We develop a TCM language model family comprising models with 4 billion, 8 billion, and 14 billion parameters. The artificial intelligence contribution is a staged clinical alignment framework integrating large scale continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, complementary reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning (RL). We further formulate herbal prescription generation as a structured RL problem with prescription-level feedback, enabling direct optimization of clinical decision outputs beyond knowledge reproduction and generic instruction following. The engineering application is TCM clinical decision support, particularly herbal prescription recommendation. We evaluate the models on a public benchmark containing 25,620 expert-verified items across 13 TCM knowledge and clinical reasoning tasks and on a private retrospective dataset of 4,348 spleen and stomach disease prescription cases. The 14 billion parameter reinforcement aligned model achieves a prescription generation F1 of 37.0 on the public benchmark, compared with 32.3 for DeepSeek-R1 with 671 billion total parameters, and a herb-level F1 of 52.8 on the clinical dataset with improved dosage agreement. Reinforcement post-training consistently improves prescription recommendation across all scales, while physician-source analysis shows that expert heterogeneity affects reward stability. These findings demonstrate a scalable pathway from domain grounding and reasoning supervision to clinically oriented prescription decision support.

Uniform Information Density-Based Preference Optimization
基于均匀信息密度的偏好优化
To enable large language models to generate outputs that align with human preferences, optimization algorithms based on the comparison between chosen and rejected output pairs have been developed and been proven effective. Some recent endeavors have utilized certain linguistically-derived assumptions about the preference pairs to guide the design of more precise optimization directions. However, human preferences are complex and hard to measure by simplistic criteria, and it is important to incorporate broader and more sophisticated insights about preferred vs. not-preferred language. In this study, we adopt a well-established psycholinguistic theory, Uniform Information Density, to develop a novel preference optimization algorithm, UIDPO. The basic assumption is that humans prefer to produce language in which information is uniformly distributed, because uniformity induces less cognitive processing effort. To implement this idea into the algorithm, we derive a compound metric for information uniformity by combining the global standard deviation and the local second-order difference, and integrate it to the objective of preference optimization. We compare UIDPO with SimPO, a previous state-of-the-art method, obtaining comparable and sometimes better performance on AlpacaEval2, ArenaHard, and MT-Bench. Additional linguistic analysis on complement clauses also shows that UIDPO can better reflect the tendencies of keeping information uniform in natural language than baselines. Our results show that the subtle human preference over the information rate in language is a helpful source for achieving better human alignment for LLMs. The code repository is published here: https://github.com/CLCS-SUSTech/UIDPO.

Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
多模态数据混合的缩放定律
Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly adopt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, as MoEs scale efficiently and partially limit cross-modal interference. We therefore use MoEs to conduct 268 experiments ranging from 457M to 8.3B parameters, on up to 150 billion tokens. Our work leads to multiple actionable insights into multimodal data mixing for training MLLMs. First, compute optima are modality-specific: audio modality is model-heavy, favoring scaling parameters over tokens, while text and vision require balanced scaling of model size and data. Second, repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x yields negligible benefits. Finally, cross-modal interactions are highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio, whereas audio's interference with learning text and vision is negligible. Overall, we provide a principled foundation for understanding the multimodal data mixtures needed to train frontier MLLMs.

Enterprise customer-support agents increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) to execute bounded, tool-using workflows. We study this problem through the lens of Skill LLMs: specialized executors that operate within a selected skill context and must complete a narrow, stateful workflow under policy and tool constraints. We find a consistent ranking in which GPT-5.4 leads by a wide margin and QWEN3.5-9B is the strongest open-weight model (below 20B), outperforming several closed baselines under every judge. We also find that judge choice is not a negligible methodological detail: pairwise judge agreement on the pass/fail verdict averages Kappa=0.524 across 10 judge pairs. These results suggest that comprehensive zero-shot evaluation of skill execution requires judge reliability as carefully as model capability.

ASSET: Adaptive Speech Segmentation via Reinforcement Learning

Speech large language models (LLMs) are often built using pretrained acoustic encoders as an audio interface to an LLM decoder. However, LLMs scale poorly with input sequence length, while acoustic encoders tend to produce substantially longer sequences than typical textual inputs. This motivates learning to compress encoder outputs while preserving task-oriented information. To this end, we introduce ASSET, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based framework that learns to adaptively compress encoder outputs by first partitioning them into variable-duration segments and then pooling each segment into a continuous audio token. We use group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) to train a segmenter with task performance feedback and a token-rate penalty. In automatic speech recognition (ASR) experiments, ASSET achieves performance comparable to a transcript-assisted character-boundary oracle with approximately 25% fewer audio tokens on English LibriSpeech, while improving on a phone-boundary oracle at a similar token rate on Mandarin AISHELL. Exploratory experiments on non-ASR tasks further illustrate how learned segmentation changes when the framework is adapted to tasks beyond transcription.

The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

Hybrid reasoning models such as the Qwen3 series switch between a THINK mode and a NO-THINK mode through a few chat-template tokens. A popular recipe trains such models with reinforcement learning in NO-THINK mode and reports improved reasoning performance. We provide evidence that much of this gain can be explained by thinking leakage: the gain comes largely from partially reactivating the reasoning abilities of the original model's THINK mode instead of learning enhanced reasoning behavior. We train Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B with GRPO in NO-THINK mode. As accuracy improves, responses become longer and more reflective, are increasingly judged by the original model to resemble its own thinking, and the model's internal activations shift toward its THINK mode. We then investigate at the level of weights, activations, and attention heads: scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches THINK-mode accuracy but does not exceed it; in Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace of the RL-trained model with its original-model value removes most of the RL gain, and the reverse exchange transfers a considerable fraction of the gain to the original model; and the RL-induced shift passes through the attention heads that read the empty think block. We further identify a possible mechanism in the GRPO training signal: responses favored by the advantage-weighted update are more THINK-like, and a gradient step computed from this signal moves the model toward its THINK state. Thus, gains in NO-THINK mode can largely reflect reactivation of reasoning abilities already present in the original model.

如通义千问Qwen3系列等混合推理模型通过少量聊天模板标记在思考模式（THINK）和非思考模式（NO-THINK）之间切换。一种流行的方法是在非思考模式下使用强化学习训练此类模型，并报告推理性能的提升。我们提供证据表明，这种性能提升很大程度上可归因于思维泄露：即性能提升主要源于部分重新激活原始模型思考模式中已有的推理能力，而非学习到更优的推理行为。我们在非思考模式下对Qwen3-1.7B、4B和8B模型使用GRPO进行训练。随着准确率提高，生成响应变得更长、更具反思性，且被原模型判断越来越像其自身的思考过程，模型内部激活也逐渐向思考模式转移。我们进一步从权重、激活和注意力头层面进行分析：进一步放大强化学习更新会激发思考模式行为，接近但无法超越思考模式的准确率；在Qwen3-8B中，将强化学习训练模型中与思考相关的低维激活子空间替换为原始模型的值，几乎消除强化学习带来的增益，而反向替换则能将相当一部分增益转移至原始模型；强化学习引起的转变会经过读取空思考块的注意力头。我们还识别出GRPO训练信号中可能的机制：优势加权更新所偏好的响应更具有思考特征，基于该信号计算的梯度步会推动模型向其思考状态靠近。因此，非思考模式下的性能提升很大程度上反映了原有模型中已存在推理能力的重新激活。

LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. Can agents use experimental feedback to progressively improve strategies, and do the resulting strategies improve target-model performance on held-out data? We study how agents use experimental feedback to develop data-engineering strategies under fixed training and evaluation protocols. Our Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework lets agents pursue, revise, or combine research directions using cumulative findings. Strategies are selected by in-loop scores and evaluated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks-math and code data selection, math reward design, and math curriculum learning-selected strategies achieve absolute gains over generic baselines of up to 13.34% on AIME25 Pass@32 and 5.85% averaged across four held-out benchmarks under fixed training conditions. In-loop scores improve over successive experiments, while held-out trajectories show that later in-loop gains do not always improve generalization. Comparisons of research organization and feedback access favor combining evidence analysis with cumulative findings. Research trajectories show how earlier findings inform strategy revisions and combinations across research directions.

Is the Future Predictable? Modeling Future Predictability for Reliable Temporal Reasoning
未来是否可预测？面向可靠时间推理的未来可预测性建模
Large language models (LLMs) remain unreliable when reasoning about the future. Existing models often overlook the difference among future states, committing to specific answers even when the queried facts are inherently volatile. To capture this challenge, we introduce ChronoRegime, a future-oriented temporal reasoning task that requires models to determine whether historical temporal evidence justifies commitment to a future answer. Furthermore, we propose Confidence-Aware Temporal Reasoning (CTR), a framework that estimates future predictability from temporal dynamics and regulates answer commitment accordingly. Rather than performing unconditional forecasting, CTR commits only when the reconstructed evidence supports the target future state. Across multiple LLMs, CTR improves strict overall accuracy by 6.7 percentage points and reduces hallucination rates by 18.4 percentage points on average over the plain QA baseline. These results demonstrate that explicit predictability assessment is an effective mechanism for safer and more reliable temporal reasoning under future uncertainty.

ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
ChunkAct：面向代理机器人的动作分块方法
Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.
中文翻译
代理机器人将大语言模型（LLM）代理置于机器人控制回路中，使其在记忆引导下组合感知、运动和视觉-语言-动作（VLA）工具，从而在无需重新训练的情况下泛化到新任务。然而，这种泛化能力带来了巨大的效率代价。每个基础动作都需要一次对完整交互历史的 LLM 推理，导致单个任务的开销随动作数量增长。我们发现这种推理大多冗余：一旦子目标选定，其后续动作已由记忆预先规定。为此，我们提出 ChunkAct，引入动作分块技术于代理机器人。在线阶段，一次调用即可启动一系列串联动作，自主执行并仅在失败时返回控制。离线阶段，ChunkAct 将记忆编译为这些分块，因此测试时无需记忆，规划器仅用于需推理的决策。LLM 计算复杂度随之从动作数量变为决策数量。在 LIBERO-Pro 上，ChunkAct 相较于当前最先进的代理机器人方法，任务成功率提升 5.0 个百分点，同时减少 2.9 倍的 LLM 调用、4.4 倍的输入 token 和 2.3 倍的输出 token。

The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
人类最后构建的遥感模型？将任何地球观测任务转化为递归自我改进
Earth observation (EO) models are still built by hand. For each new task, experts design a training recipe and tune it against a benchmark. We show that this loop can be handed to an agent. Any verifiable task can be cast as a harness and a verifier, where the harness defines what the agent may use and the verifier defines what counts as success. Every EO task can be made verifiable, through labeled benchmarks, independent sensors, physical models or the repeated observation of the same place. Given only these two components, a general-purpose coding agent builds the EO model and improves it recursively on its own outputs. Settings long treated as separate research problems, from learning with a handful of labels to adapting across domains, become choices of harness and verifier. On four EO benchmarks spanning optical, SAR and multispectral time-series imagery, agent-built models surpass the state of the art and keep most of that accuracy from about 1% of the training labels. This establishes a new paradigm for EO, in which people design harnesses and verifiers and agents build the models, so EO models improve as agents do.

Self-Evolving Agent Harness
自演化智能体约束器
Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. We characterize search through evolutionary optimization and examine its reliability through continual PAC-learning. Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data. We examine how persistent harness revisions affect knowledge sharing and organizational workflows, with implications for scientific reliability, physical safety, and institutional accountability. Cases from prior work illustrate model--harness co-design, distributed execution, and plugin reuse. Reliable deployment requires continual validation as task distributions and evaluators change, with independent safeguards for learning, runtime privileges, and consequential actions. We provide a comprehensive 66-page discussion of related work, theory, algorithms, evaluation, applications, and the broader impact of Harness RSI, together with continuously updated code and supplementary materials, at https://github.com/zgcagi/Harness-RSI.

SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
SkillScaffold：基于策略自适应技能信用分配与选择性注入的智能体强化学习支架
Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from multi-turn interactions with verifiable outcomes. Textual skills can improve exploration by distilling prior interactions into reusable guidance. However, existing skill-based RL approaches often either assume skill injection is beneficial or rely on indirect feedback or rollout-intensive evaluation to assess its utility. Our pilot studies show that rollout-based utility estimation for skill credit assignment is costly and unstable under limited sampling, while skill benefits vary across candidates and depend on the current policy's competence on each query. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillScaffold, a policy-adaptive training scaffold that combines low-cost skill-utility estimation with selective skill injection. By reusing outcome-verified training trajectories, SkillScaffold generates candidate skills and estimates their utility through outcome-aware likelihood comparisons, without candidate-specific environment rollouts. The resulting utility guides whether and which skill to inject, retaining skill-free execution when no candidate is estimated to help. Joint training enables the Generator to produce skills tailored to the evolving Executor. Scaffolded RL encourages skill internalization for skill-free inference. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and $τ^2$-Bench demonstrate gains over strong agentic-RL and skill-based RL baselines across both short- and long-horizon tasks. Ablations and further analyses support the importance of utility-based selection and abstention. Our code is available at https://github.com/Vaidurya00/SkillScaffold.
中文翻译
智能体强化学习（RL）使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够从具有可验证结果的多轮交互中学习。文本形式的技能可通过将先前交互提炼为可重用指导来改善探索。然而，现有基于技能的RL方法通常要么假设技能注入有益，要么依赖间接反馈或耗时的回溯评估来判断其效用。我们的初步研究表明，在样本有限的情况下，基于回溯的技能信用估计成本高且不稳定，且技能收益因候选项而异，且取决于当前策略在每项查询上的能力。为解决这些挑战，我们提出SkillScaffold，一种策略自适应的训练支架，结合低成本的技能效用估计与选择性技能注入。通过重用已验证结果的训练轨迹，SkillScaffold在无需为每个候选环境回溯的情况下，通过结果感知的概率比较生成候选技能并估计其效用。由此产生的效用决定是否以及注入哪个技能，当无候选技能被估计为有益时则保留无技能执行。联合训练使生成器能够生成适配不断演进的执行器的技能。支架化的RL鼓励技能内化，以实现无技能推理。在ALFWorld、WebShop、ScienceWorld和$τ^2$-Bench上的实验表明，SkillScaffold在短周期和长周期任务上均优于强基线的智能体RL和基于技能的RL方法。消融实验和进一步分析支持基于效用的选择与放弃的重要性。代码已公开于 https://github.com/Vaidurya00/SkillScaffold。

Pre-trained Large Language Model (LLMs) are effective on many tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings. For machine translation of low-resource languages, the obvious options are few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on a small parallel set. We ask: what if moderate amounts of low-resource monolingual data are also available? We argue that, rather than continued pretraining, a more effective use of this data is the pre-LLM era technique of back-translation (BT). The current fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences in each language, and the resulting pairs train it in the reverse direction. Updates on the parallel set are interleaved for stable learning. With 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, BT beats continued pretraining into the low-resource language by 7.7 to 16.4 XCOMET-XXL points in domain. With beam-decoded intermediate translations, it also beats a model with 10 time more parallel data. In-context examples retrieved from the parallel data further improve BT. We also analyze the source, quality and amount of monolingual text. Across five low-resource languages, with Hindi as a high-resource control, and two 3B backbones, BT improves translation into the low-resource language by 16 to 173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning. Blind human evaluation on Odia and Sanskrit agrees with the automatic metrics.

We also find that surprisal values for sub-lexical units are predictive of pupil dilation. 虚拟头注意力机制
The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.

Swiss4Arg: A Parallel Dataset for Multilingual Argument Mining across Swiss National Languages
Swiss4Arg：面向瑞士四种官方语言的多语言论点挖掘并行数据集
We present Swiss4Arg, a multilingual dataset for argument mining based on official Swiss voting brochures, covering all four national languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh (a Romance minority language exclusively spoken in Switzerland). The brochures contain explicitly formulated arguments systematically organized into pro and con sections, resulting in a cross-lingually aligned resource with balanced argumentative stance. We create a dataset that comprises 53 federal voting issues collected between 2019 and 2025, annotated for argument components (major claims, claims, premises, and non-argumentative units) and relations (support and attack) by three native speakers per language. Inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha) reaches 0.548 for component classification and 0.623 for relation and target classification, computed jointly across all annotators on the parallel data. We release both adjudicated labels and individual annotator annotations, enabling analyses of disagreement and cross-linguistic variation, and provide baseline results using GPT-5.4 and SwissBERT. Swiss4Arg establishes a novel benchmark for multilingual argument mining, with a particular focus on cross-lingual comparability and low-resource settings such as Romansh. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://anonymous-hf.up.railway.app/a/gozw0nion72y/ (HuggingFace) and https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MultiVote-03BD/ (GitHub).
中文翻译
我们提出了Swiss4Arg，一个基于瑞士官方投票宣传册的多语言论点挖掘数据集，涵盖德语、法语、意大利语和罗曼什语（瑞士独有的罗曼语少数语言）四种官方语言。这些宣传册系统性地将论点分为支持与反对两部分，形成跨语言对齐且立场平衡的资源。我们构建了一个包含2019至2025年间53个联邦投票议题的数据集，由每种语言三位母语者标注论点组件（主要主张、主张、前提及非论点单元）和关系（支持与攻击）。跨所有标注者的互评一致性（Krippendorff's alpha）在组件分类上达到0.548，在关系与目标分类上为0.623。我们公开了经裁定的标签和各标注者原始标注，以支持分歧分析与跨语言差异研究，并提供了基于GPT-5.4和SwissBERT的基线结果。Swiss4Arg为多语言论点挖掘建立了新基准，尤其关注跨语言可比性与低资源场景（如罗曼什语）。数据集与代码已公开于https://anonymous-hf.up.railway.app/a/gozw0nion72y/（HuggingFace）和https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MultiVote-03BD/（GitHub）。
👤 Sophia Conrad, Fatma-Zohra Rezkellah, Christina Niklaus, Reto Gubelmann 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17778]
GENDIS: Gender-Related Discourse and Stance in Multilingual YouTube Comments from India, Kenya, and Nigeria
GENDIS：印度、肯尼亚和尼日利亚多语言YouTube评论中的性别相关话语与立场分析
Research on gender-related online content is often operationalized through harm-centered tasks that collapse non-harmful gender-related and unrelated content, while existing datasets remain concentrated in high-resource languages and Global North settings. To bridge these gaps, we introduce GENDIS, a dataset of 9,600 multilingual, human-annotated YouTube comments from India, Kenya, and Nigeria (3,200 per country), annotated using a two-level framework that first identifies whether gender is referenced and then classifies gender-related content as negative, positive, or neutral. This separation provides a denominator for gender-related discourse independent of harm, enabling both prevalence estimation and characterization of its evaluative range. In the uniform random stratum, 23.8-35.0% of comments are gender-related, and among those with a resolved stance, 82% are neutral or positive. Across models, gender-reference detection is substantially easier than stance classification, especially for positive and neutral speech. Lightly supervised classifiers match frontier zero-shot large language models at substantially lower cost and outperform generic toxicity detection, while cross-country transfer remains limited. GENDIS provides a locally grounded resource for measuring when gender is invoked online and how that reference is framed.
中文翻译
关于性别相关网络内容的研究通常以伤害为中心的任务来操作，导致非伤害性性别相关内容与无关内容被混同；且现有数据集仍集中于高资源语言和全球北方地区。为弥合这些差距，我们引入GENDIS，一个包含9,600条多语言、人工标注的YouTube评论的数据集（每国3,200条），采用两级标注框架：首先判断是否提及性别，再将性别相关内容分类为负面、正面或中性。这种分离方式提供了不依赖于伤害性的性别话语基数，从而支持流行度估算及评价范围的刻画。在均匀随机子样本中，23.8%至35.0%的评论涉及性别，其中具有明确立场的评论中，82%为中性或正面。在各类模型中，性别提及检测远比立场分类容易，尤其对正面和中性言论而言。轻量监督分类器以更低的成本达到前沿零样本大语言模型的性能，并优于通用毒性检测模型，但跨国家迁移能力有限。GENDIS为衡量在线环境中何时提及性别及其表述方式提供了本地化基础资源。
👤 Luise Koch, Manuel Tonneau, Niyati Malhotra, Sunny Rai, Ana Maria Munoz Boudet et al. 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17761]
Connecting the Dots: Enduring Performance Gaps in ASR Systems Between Standard and Minority English Varieties
连接线索：标准英语与少数族裔英语变体之间ASR系统性能差距的持续存在
Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system evaluations have consistently revealed performance disparities along lines of race, gender, socioeconomic status, and language variety. While these disparities are well-documented, they are often (implicitly or explicitly) treated as issues that subsequent, larger, and more universal models will correct. We challenge this assumption of steady progress in reducing accent-related performance disparities, conducting a longitudinal evaluation of 16 prominent systems released between 2021-2025 across 8 datasets representing diverse English accent varieties. We find that the performance disparity between Mainstream US English (MUSE) and minority accents is stubborn, not reliably declining as a function of time. Specifically, while systems are reliably performant on MUSE, minority accents are subject to risks of large performance degradations between generations of systems, sometimes worsening by 65% absolute Word Error Rate. We argue that standard ASR benchmarks enact an implicit language policy privileging Mainstream US English varieties. As such, these performance disparities reflect systemic failures of language technology development infrastructure that disproportionately affect underrepresented speaker populations.
中文翻译
自动语音识别（ASR）系统的评估始终揭示出在种族、性别、社会经济地位和语言变体方面的性能差异。尽管这些差异已被广泛记录，但常被隐含或明确视为后续更大、更通用的模型将自行纠正的问题。我们挑战了这种关于减少口音相关性能差距将持续进步的假设，对2021至2025年间发布的16个主流ASR系统进行了纵向评估，涵盖8个代表多样化英语口音变体的数据集。研究发现，主流美国英语（MUSE）与少数族裔口音之间的性能差距顽固存在，并未随时间可靠下降。具体而言，虽然系统在MUSE上表现稳定，但少数族裔口音在系统代际间面临严重的性能退化风险，有时词错误率（WER）绝对值上升高达65%。我们认为，标准ASR基准实际上执行了一种隐含的语言政策，偏袒主流美国英语变体。因此，这些性能差距反映了语言技术开发基础设施的系统性失败，对代表性不足的说话者群体造成了不成比例的影响。
👤 Alexander Metzger, Aruna Srivastava, Ruslan Mukhamedvaleev, Eunjung Yeo, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed et al. 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17742]
Geometric Structure Predicts Per-Example Neighborhood Loss Under PCA Truncation
几何结构预测PCA截断下的单例邻域损失
Dimensionality reduction can preserve the average performance of text embeddings even when a substantial fraction of their dimensions is removed. Aggregate metrics, however, do not reveal whether degradation is distributed uniformly across examples. We study per-example neighborhood stability under PCA truncation across static word embeddings and modern sentence encoders. Per-item neighbor retention varies widely and is predictable from geometric properties of the representation and its alignment with the retained PCA subspace. The fraction of centered-vector energy retained by the truncated subspace is strongest for CBOW and RI, with neighborhood contrast leading on SkipGram and the modern/Matryoshka settings (GTE approximately tied), while local density is associated with retention in marginal analysis but adds little unique information once energy and contrast are controlled (R-squared increments 0.001 to 0.010). Local intrinsic dimensionality accounts for more variation than density on modern sentence encoders in pairwise comparison. On SciFact, query density predicts retrieval degradation under aggressive compression; on NFCorpus the primary 32d association does not replicate, and a direct variance-restriction test leaves that null unresolved. Average compression performance conceals systematic per-example variation that geometry makes visible.
中文翻译
降维技术可在移除大量维度的情况下仍保持文本嵌入的平均性能。然而，整体指标无法揭示退化是否在各实例间均匀分布。我们研究了静态词嵌入和现代句向量编码器在PCA截断下的单例邻域稳定性。单个实例的邻居保留率差异显著，且可由表示的几何特性及其与保留PCA子空间的对齐程度预测。截断子空间保留的中心向量能量占比在CBOW和RI中最强，而邻域对比度在SkipGram及现代/Matryoshka设置（GTE近似持平）中占优；局部密度在边际分析中与保留相关，但在控制能量和对比度后贡献极小（R²增量0.001至0.010）。在现代句向量编码器中，局部内在维度在成对比较中解释的变异比密度更多。在SciFact数据集上，查询密度可预测激进压缩下的检索退化；在NFCorpus上，主32维关联未能复现，直接方差约束测试也未能解决该空结果。平均压缩性能掩盖了由几何结构揭示的系统性单例差异。

[2610.17731]
Understanding Machine Taste: Aesthetic Agreement Across Foundation Models in K-pop
理解机器品味：基础模型在K-pop中的审美一致性研究
As foundation models enter creative industries, understanding their aesthetic preferences becomes an important step toward AI-assisted creative decision making. In this work, we investigate how foundation models evaluate creative content and characterize their ``machine taste'' using K-pop songs and music videos as a testbed. We formulate aesthetic evaluation as a pairwise ranking problem and systematically examine pairwise inter-model agreement, group-level consensus, and cross-modal preference alignment. Our results reveal stronger pairwise inter-model agreement and group-level consensus in visual evaluation than in audio evaluation, while preferences across the two modalities remain weakly aligned. We further examine how visual consensus rankings relate to real-world popularity using historical YouTube viewership data, finding positive but varying correlations across artist groups. These findings provide initial insights into machine aesthetic preferences and lay the groundwork for future AI-assisted creative decision making that considers creative content, artist identity, audience preferences, and market dynamics.
中文翻译
随着基础模型进入创意产业，理解其审美偏好成为实现AI辅助创意决策的重要一步。本文以K-pop歌曲和音乐视频为实验场景，探究基础模型如何评估创意内容，并刻画其‘机器品味’。我们将审美评价建模为成对排序问题，系统性地考察模型间的成对一致性、群体层面共识以及跨模态偏好对齐。研究结果表明，在视觉评价中，模型间的成对一致性与群体共识更强，而音频与视觉评价之间的偏好仍弱度对齐。我们进一步分析视觉共识排名与现实世界流行度的关系，利用历史YouTube观看数据发现，不同艺人组别间存在正向但变化的关联。这些发现为机器审美偏好提供了初步洞察，也为未来考虑创意内容、艺术家身份、受众偏好与市场动态的AI辅助创意决策奠定了基础。

[2610.17703]
Pushback in a Haystack: Language Models Respond to Factual Errors Ambiguously and Ineffectively
在 haystack 中的反驳：语言模型对事实错误的回应模糊且无效
The sycophancy of language models, or their failure to push back against faulty user input, is now widely studied. However, if LMs do push back, is sycophancy solved? We show that LMs vary in how they present pushback, and thus vary in how effectively they correct user beliefs. We introduce a phrase-level, human-validated response labeling framework to uncover fine-grained insights into how LMs push against and/or affirm false inputs. We develop and apply our framework on model responses in five languages: English, German, Chinese, Hindi, and Yoruba. We find that when models do push back against users' false assertions, they tend to use indirect phrasing and mix in affirmation, with more indirectness in Hindi and Yoruba than in other languages considered. In a large-scale human study (n = 300), we find that the pushback ambiguity we identified may fail to correct and prevent users' factual misconceptions.
中文翻译
语言模型的阿谀奉承现象，即其未能对用户输入中的错误进行反驳，如今已被广泛研究。然而，如果语言模型确实进行了反驳，是否就解决了阿谀奉承问题？我们发现，语言模型在呈现反驳方式上存在差异，因此在纠正用户错误信念方面的有效性也各不相同。我们引入了一个基于短语级别的、经人工验证的响应标注框架，以揭示语言模型如何对错误输入进行反驳和/或确认的细微洞察。我们在五种语言（英语、德语、汉语、印地语和约鲁巴语）的语言模型响应中开发并应用了该框架。研究发现，当模型对用户的错误断言进行反驳时，倾向于使用间接表达并混合确认，其中印地语和约鲁巴语的间接性更强。在一项大规模人类研究（n = 300）中，我们发现所识别出的反驳模糊性可能无法纠正并防止用户形成事实误解。

[2610.17658]
Worth Their Weights? Evaluating Generative Models for Discourse Parsing
值得它们的权重吗？评估生成式模型在话语解析中的表现
Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) parsing has historically been dominated by discriminative models based on pretrained encoder-only language models. The recent availability of high-quality generative language models has made it unclear whether RST parsing is better approached as a generative task. In this work, we investigate whether generative language models are better at parsing RST than traditional discriminative ones. We find that at matched parameter counts, discriminative parsers perform much better than generative ones, though much larger generative models sometimes outperform them. Generative models hold a particular advantage in elementary discourse unit (EDU) segmentation, and we report new state-of-the-art results on the RST-DT benchmark in end-to-end parsing as well as segmentation.
中文翻译
修辞结构理论（RST）解析长期以来由基于预训练编码器的语言模型的判别式模型主导。近年来高质量生成式语言模型的出现，使得RST解析是否应作为生成任务尚不明确。本文研究生成式语言模型在RST解析方面是否优于传统判别式模型。我们发现，在参数量相当的情况下，判别式解析器的表现远超生成式模型，尽管更大规模的生成式模型有时能超越判别式模型。生成式模型在基本话语单元（EDU）分割方面具有特殊优势，并在端到端解析以及分割任务上报告了RST-DT基准的新最佳结果。

[2610.17654]
Decouple to Forget: Semantic Mediation for Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
解耦遗忘：大语言模型中敏感信息遗忘的语义中介方法
Machine unlearning for large language models seeks to remove specified knowledge while preserving general capability, yet current methods often treat an entire response as the unit of forgetting. This coarse granularity causes unnecessary utility loss when the forget target is only a small set of sensitive facts embedded within otherwise benign explanations. In this paper, we introduce Decouple to Forget (D2F), a targeted unlearning method inspired by semantic mediation that separates sensitive factual content from non-sensitive meaning and surface expression. For each example to be forgotten, D2F extracts a fact-level "mediator" representation from the answer, identifies which parts are sensitive, and removes only those parts while leaving the rest of the structure intact. We then generate counterfactual answers grounded in this mediator that preserve non-sensitive content but exclude sensitive facts, employing preference-based contrastive optimization to reduce the likelihood of information leakage while maintaining helpfulness and fluency. Experiments across various benchmark datasets show that D2F achieves a better balance between forgetting and retention than strong baseline methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/JingyueCong/D2F.
中文翻译
大语言模型的机器遗忘旨在移除特定知识的同时保持通用能力，但现有方法通常将整个响应视为遗忘单位。这种粗粒度处理在仅需遗忘嵌入于无害解释中的少量敏感事实时，会导致不必要的性能损失。本文提出Decouple to Forget（D2F）方法，受语义中介启发，将敏感事实内容与非敏感语义及表面表达分离。对于每个需遗忘的示例，D2F从回答中提取事实级别的“中介”表示，识别出敏感部分并仅移除这些部分，同时保留其余结构。随后，基于该中介生成反事实回答，保留非敏感内容但排除敏感事实，并采用基于偏好对比优化的方法降低信息泄露概率，同时维持有用性和流畅性。在多个基准数据集上的实验表明，D2F在遗忘与保留之间取得了优于强基线方法的平衡。代码已公开于 https://github.com/JingyueCong/D2F。
👤 Jingyue Cong, Andy Song, Yang Yu, Tabinda Sarwar, Xinshu Li et al. 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17597]
TDR: Tagalog Diacritic Restoration Dataset
TDR：他加禄语变音符号恢复数据集
Homographs are words that share identical spelling but differ in meaning and pronunciation. In Tagalog, these distinctions are disambiguated in writing through tuldik (diacritical marks), which are rarely preserved in contemporary Tagalog text. This scarcity of diacritics limits diacritic restoration, which is useful for downstream tasks such as prosody selection for text-to-speech synthesis. To address this gap, this study introduces TDR, an annotated corpus of 40 frequent Tagalog homographs constructed from news text. It also introduces a collocation-driven retrieval method to expand the dataset and mitigate severe class imbalance among minor variants. Finally, we show that TDR supplies a capability absent from pretrained models, and that this capability can be learned by small, inexpensive models as well as by fine-tuned LLMs.
中文翻译
同形异义词是指拼写相同但意义和发音不同的词语。在他加禄语中，这些区别通过tuldik（变音符号）在书写中加以区分，但在当代他加禄语文本中这些符号很少被保留。这种变音符号的缺失限制了变音符号恢复任务，而该任务对语音合成中的韵律选择等下游任务具有重要意义。为此，本研究构建了TDR，一个由新闻文本中40个常见他加禄语同形异义词组成的标注语料库。同时提出一种基于搭配的检索方法以扩展数据集，并缓解少数变体间的严重类别不平衡问题。最后，我们展示了TDR为预训练模型所不具备的能力，并且该能力可由小型廉价模型以及微调的大语言模型学习到。
👤 Ivan Yuri De Leon, Lanz Railey Fermin, Zachary Aldridge Africa, Richell Isaiah Flores 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17538]
Everyone Was Right: Lexical Representations in Language Models Are Both Abstract and Holistic
人人皆对：语言模型中的词汇表征既抽象又整体
Lexical representations can encode both abstract information and information specific to particular contexts. We investigate how these forms of information are organized in language models by decomposing contextual word representations into item, class, and word-class interaction components. Across six pretrained transformers and two linguistic categories, we find that the interaction is consistently present, grows across layers, and contains information associated with both item and class. Unlike the nearly orthogonal item and class effects, the interaction overlaps with both and encodes class information beyond the shared class effect. An interaction also emerges in artificial-language learners even when the input contains only additive structure. Together, these findings show that lexical representations combine abstract information with structure specific to particular word-class combinations.
中文翻译
词汇表征可以编码抽象信息以及特定于具体语境的信息。我们通过将上下文词表示分解为项目、类别及词类交互成分，研究这些信息在语言模型中的组织方式。在六个预训练Transformer模型和两个语言类别中，我们发现交互成分始终存在，随层加深而增强，并包含与项目和类别相关的信息。与几乎正交的项目和类别效应不同，交互成分与两者均有重叠，并编码超出共享类别效应的类别信息。即使输入仅含加法结构，人工语言学习者中也出现了交互成分。这些发现共同表明，词汇表征结合了抽象信息与特定词类组合的结构特征。
👤 Zachary Nicholas Houghton, Yu Zhou, Dan Pluth, Vijay K. Gurbani, Vsevolod Kapatsinski 📅 2026-10-13 🔗 arXiv
[2610.17461]
Distilling Text LMs into Speech-to-Speech LMs by Matching Internal Text Predictions
通过匹配内部文本预测将文本语言模型蒸馏为语音到语音语言模型
Text language models (LMs) acquire broad linguistic and factual capabilities through large-scale pretraining, while comparable capabilities remain difficult to learn from speech alone. Recent work has shown that knowledge distillation from pretrained text LMs offers a promising way to transfer their linguistic and factual capabilities to speech models. However, existing distillation approaches have largely focused on speech-input, text-output models. This idea has yet to be explored for {\it speech-to-speech} models, which operate on both speech input and speech output. In this work we introduce a speech-to-speech pretraining method that creates an internal text interface for knowledge transfer while preserving the speech-only input and output. The model first consumes speech context without its transcription, switches to text prediction, and then uses the predicted text to lead future speech generation word by word. It also provides an interface for knowledge distillation: the internal text predictions can be directly distilled from the base text LM. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of text LM distillation to a speech-to-speech LM. Under matched training conditions, the proposed sequence construction substantially improves the generative perplexity of spoken continuations over speech-only and interleaved speech-text models, approaching the performance of a text-leading inner-monologue model with external ASR prompt transcription. More importantly, distillation improves factual performance under both text and speech evaluation, indicating better retention of knowledge from the base text language model.
中文翻译

AI-generated outputs are frequently perceived as highly creative, but also tend to be more similar to each other (homogenized) than human ideas. Does the human heterogeneity that extends beyond AI reflect valuable thinking that AI misses? Alternatively, is greater human heterogeneity driven by lower-quality ideas and less effective thinking that AI avoids? We developed Expansion of Divergent Generative Expression (EDGE) to map AI's semantic "blind spots" by assessing how strongly/weakly individual human ideas were represented in a task-matched AI semantic comparison set. Specifically, we compared human-generated vs. AI-generated ideas across three open-ended tasks: college admissions essays, alternative uses for everyday objects, and interpersonal advice. Across all three tasks, human responses extended into semantic regions sparsely covered by AI outputs. These distinctively human responses showed no meaningful deficits in creativity, quality, or effectiveness, were associated with equal-or-better academic performance, and with credibly superior ratings and achievement for some outcomes. These ideas were thus not merely poor-performing variation; they performed as well as or better than ideas that overlapped more strongly with AI ideas. More distinctive human ideas tended to receive higher creativity ratings, but this relationship was weak or reversed for AI ideas. Taken together, these results suggest that differentiation among human-generated ideas does not reflect poor thinking that AI can safely omit, and instead may afford both individual and population-level advantages.

Sampling multiple reports creates an inference problem: how should sampled evidence be converted into a final decision, and does a better structured decision yield a better report? We study these questions through a framework that separates the decision signal, scoring objective, and feasible decision set, followed by text realization. On MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray, controlled comparisons across 13 generator configurations per benchmark under grouped development/test evaluation reveal three findings. First, changing the objective under fixed evidence and rule capacity changes predictions and their held-out metric trade-offs. Second, relaxing candidate constraints has objective-dependent effects under shared signals and frozen scores. Diagnostics connect the IU macro-oriented assertion increase to near-zero label thresholds and show that limited candidate coverage coexists with selection headroom. Third, a controlled realization study with SFT-Qwen3-VL-8B shows that decision-level gains can be attenuated, amplified, or reversed. Change decomposition reveals that realization can remove incorrect assertions while losing correct findings, so target fidelity and reference accuracy need not improve together. Finding gains also do not consistently improve reference-based report quality. These results motivate separate evaluation of decision rules, candidate constraints, and realized reports.

The original EneMonIE proposal describes a Web-based semantic system for continuously monitoring energy trends through targeted information extraction from heterogeneous online media. This article presents EneMonIE-Backend, an implementation-derived redesign that converts that conceptual pipeline into a modular, executable, and application-independent backend. The architecture separates five concerns: data sources, acquisition and normalization, semantic processing, knowledge organization, and persistent storage. It operationalizes configurable connectors for RSS feeds, URL collections, arXiv, social-media JSON files, and open-data CSV files; it also introduces question-driven Web search and scraping. Relevant documents pass through energy categorization, named entity recognition, temporal and event extraction, source sensitive sentiment analysis, and extractive summarization. The resulting semantic representations support entity co-occurrence graphs, cross-document interlinking, cluster-level information fusion, and relational persistence in SQLite. Three grounded question-answering paths are exposed at the backend level: live Web evidence, the stored corpus, and selected configured resources. Answer generation uses a language model when configured and otherwise falls back to deterministic extractive output. Unlike the original proposal, the presented architecture deliberately excludes the user-interface and server-side application layers, allowing the semantic core to be embedded in different applications. A deterministic smoke validation confirms relevance filtering, persistence, clustering, evidence retrieval, and document deletion. The work provides a reproducible architectural basis for future evaluation on larger multilingual energy corpora.

Gluing Local Contexts into Global Meaning: A Sheaf-Theoretic Decomposition of Transformer Representations

Existing interpretability tools do not test whether a representation keeps the same content when only the phrasing changes. We treat each paraphrase pair as a local witness that two activations should agree and build a cellular sheaf over the paraphrase graph; its Laplacian $L_\mathcal{F}$ answers the question on a frozen model with no training. The kernel $H^0$ is a content subspace: at 20 dimensions it beats the preserved subspace of the concept eraser LEACE on held-out CounterFact fact retrieval across eight architectures by a mean $+17.1$\,pp, and constraining all paraphrases of a fact jointly adds a further $+6.5$\,pp. The spectral complement concentrates causal influence: ablating the most paraphrase-variable coordinates, a coordinate-wise proxy for it, changes model outputs $5.6$ to $26.5\times$ more than ablating coordinates of matched per-coordinate variability, across nine models from 124M to 13B parameters. Stacking layers into a grid creates $b_1 = N(L-1)$ algebraic 1-cycles, and the resulting model-derived harmonic mass varies by nearly three orders of magnitude across six architectures and ranks them as their steering fragility does (Spearman $ρ= 0.90$, exact one-sided permutation $p = 0.014$). The same paraphrase graph yields the content subspace, the influence directions, and the fragility measure. Project page: https://cwru-aism.github.io/gluing-lc-page/

Information extraction models often perform well on the datasets they are trained on, but transferring to new domains and annotation guidelines remains challenging. Supporting user-specified types alone does not resolve this problem. We present CalOn, a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction across datasets and schemas. The model jointly encodes text and type definitions, then directly identifies entity spans, relations between spans, and event triggers and arguments. Its extraction decisions consider the requested types together, using their combined evidence to identify relevant candidates before assigning a type. This gives all three tasks a common probabilistic formulation while keeping every extracted mention anchored to the input text. We train on diverse sources, and supplement supervised learning with a reward that encourages correct extractions and penalises incorrect ones. Across 40 benchmarks, CalOn outperforms the evaluated baselines on most benchmarks. It leads all reported relation extraction benchmarks and achieves the highest average F1 for event triggers and arguments with gold triggers. The same model also performs strongly on aspect sentiment triplet extraction and pronoun resolution through its span-pair formulation. A correction for the probability bias introduced during training improves confidence estimates for entities, relations, and event arguments after calibration, with little change in F1.

Online discussions on platforms like Reddit are a productive testbed for fallacy detection: short texts, broad topical range, and the full inventory of informal fallacies. The Touche 2026 lab at CLEF formalises this as a shared task on a Reddit-derived corpus that combines fallacy detection with argument-scheme classification. This paper describes our participation in all three subtasks (ST1 binary fallacy detection, ST2 eight-way fallacy classification, ST3 four-way argument-scheme classification) and both evaluation tracks. Our submitted systems are fine-tuned RoBERTa-large encoders with task-specific heads, augmented with a small batch of LLM-generated synthetic contrastive pairs; for ST2 and ST3 on the enhanced track we additionally added confidence-filtered pseudo-labelled examples from the unlabelled pool. A wider backbone comparison spanning additional encoders (DeBERTa-v3, ModernBERT) and an LLM track (four Qwen variants from 3B to 32B, zero-shot through CoT-LoRA) showed no validated benefit over RoBERTa-large at this corpus scale, with 5-fold variance wide enough that we call the comparison underpowered rather than settled. We also characterise how much of the enhanced track's lift reflects organiser-rewritten inputs carrying label information rather than genuine argument clarification. On the official Touche 2026 test set our systems ranked first on both base-track classification cells (ST2 and ST3) and second on both binary-detection (ST1) tracks, with the two enhanced-track classification cells topped by cascaded and multitask systems. We close with the rare-class limitation on ST3 and the most useful follow-ups. Code: https://github.com/psychias/fallacy_detection_clef_2026

Most prior work on predicting mental health help-seeking treats it as post-hoc classification of users already active in clinical communities, which cannot tell whether someone approaching a transition can be identified in advance. We instead frame help-seeking as a time-to-event problem and ask which Reddit users will eventually seek mental health support, and how imminent that transition is. We build a two-arm cohort: a control frame of 6,337 ordinary users with genuine right-censoring (12.1% transition rate) to answer who will transition, and a clinical frame of 5,023 eventual transitioners to answer how soon. Features come only from posts written before any clinical activity, and user-grouped five-fold cross-validation plus a four-year temporal holdout guard against leakage. We compare TF-IDF, MentalBERT embeddings and behavioural activity features using Cox proportional hazards models, Random Survival Forests and an LSTM sequential model. Behavioural features alone outperform text for predicting who will seek help (C-index 0.797 vs. 0.763), and combining both is best (0.823 under cross-validation, 0.856 on the holdout). The pattern reverses for predicting how soon a known transition will happen: text remains a stable predictor (C-index 0.698) while behavioural features become unstable. Recent work has investigated Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs), models which can take multiple modalities and their combinations as input, as a way forward to have systems really capable of interacting with their environment. On UNO-Bench, with both a closed and an open model, our scores yield small gains over self-consistency (systematic with the closed generator, mixed with the open one) and are competitive with self-verbalisation and internal-state baselines, especially in open-ended, omni-modal questions where previous state-of-the-art baselines struggle.

近期研究探索了多模态大语言模型（OLLMs），即能够接受多种模态及其组合输入的模型，以实现真正与环境交互的系统。然而，OLLMs的不确定性量化（UQ）仍是一个开放问题：现有方法大多仅针对最多两种模态，需要访问模型内部信息或重新调用被评估模型。我们提出了一种无需依赖模型本身的UQ框架，完全通过外部多模态嵌入对思维链（Chain-of-Thought）响应进行评分，衡量推理在多模态输入中的根基性及其内部一致性。我们的贡献在于信号族的构建和其可靠性经验表征，而非单一估计器：我们发现几何评分彼此高度冗余（分组内秩相关系数0.91-0.94），但与答案离散度基线具有强互补性，且其可靠性取决于生成器和模态类型。所得置信度估计无需访问被评估模型的logits、隐藏状态或梯度，也无需额外推理；但需要借助辅助模型对推理轨迹进行分割，并为聚合评分提供一个标注校准集，我们证明该集合可小至25个样本（尽管我们也显示，预先固定某一信号的收益有限）。在UNO-Bench上，无论是封闭模型还是开放模型，我们的评分均在自洽性基础上取得小幅提升（封闭生成器下系统性提升，开放生成器下结果混合），并可与自言自语和内部状态基线相媲美，尤其在开放式多模态问题中表现优异，而此前的最先进基线在此类任务中表现不佳。

Parallel token proposals in language-model decoding need a joint law, not merely accurate token marginals. We construct a family of coordinate-Bethe-ansatz laws from the periodic XXZ chain and compare each with its maximum-entropy pairwise projection at identical one- and two-site moments. In the eight-site, three-excitation sector, symmetry makes their entire probability-law difference one-dimensional, determined by a contiguous three-site moment. Along the Bethe branch, this gap varies with anisotropy, changes sign, and vanishes exactly at $Δ=(3+\sqrt{3})/2$, where the eigenstate law becomes exactly pairwise. A nonlinear readout transfers a nonzero gap into the first two token positions while preserving their separate marginals. At $Δ=1.5$ the deterministic binary token laws differ by 0.02654573 in total variation. Specifically, we aim to understand whether multilingual LLM-generated text is also homogeneous, and whether this homogeneity matches what we observe in humans. Machine translation (MT) is increasingly utilized in multilingual crisis communication, yet conventional evaluation does not directly assess whether translated emergency messages preserve their actionability. We introduce SIREN (Situation-aware Index for Response and Emergency ActioNability), a human evaluation framework assessing whether translation choices compromise protective action, directive force, and urgency of the source text. We evaluate SIREN in two complementary settings. At the error level, we apply it to HOPE-annotated Italian--English translations produced by ChatGPT-4o and Google Translate: 31.63\% and 48.73\% of errors, respectively, compromise actionability, predominantly by affecting the protective action. At the message level, we evaluate English--French translations produced by TranslateGemma-4B and Google Translate, with actionability preserved in 85.34\% and 92.67\% of translations, respectively. TranslateGemma-4B failures predominantly weaken directive force, whereas Google Translate failures more often compromise protective actions and receive Major impact ratings. These findings show that translation systems can differ not only in how often actionability is lost, but also in the nature and functional impact of these failures. Alongside SIREN, we contribute an English--French crisis-translation resource with human actionability annotations and post-edited reference translations, supporting further research on function-oriented evaluation for crisis communication. Our experimental data is available at https://github.com/mcstaiano/SIREN.

For monolingual identification, MixLID outperforms all baselines in both accuracy and macro F1 on four benchmarks within the language coverage shared with each baseline. Support or Magnitude? Characterizing Neuron Relevance for Instruction Data Selection

Model-internal signals, such as neuron activations and gradients, have been used for instruction data selection, yet how neuron relevance should be characterized remains underexplored. In particular, should selection prioritize the magnitude of relevance or how broadly it is distributed across neurons? To investigate this question, we construct sample-level relevance profiles using AttnLRP-guided attribution and introduce two complementary criteria: Effective Relevance Support (ERS), which measures the effective support of positive relevance, and Positive Relevance Magnitude (PRM), which captures its average strength. Our analyses reveal that these characterizations produce distinct sample rankings and selection preferences despite sharing the same underlying relevance profiles. On Qwen2 models, PRM exhibits stronger associations with activation-based selection, whereas ERS produces substantially different rankings. These differences extend to task composition, within-task sample preferences, and semantic selection patterns, with varying degrees of agreement across backbones. Experiments across three language models and five downstream benchmarks demonstrate the practical value of relevance-guided selection, with ERS achieving the best overall average performance rank among the evaluated methods. Our findings highlight that how neuron relevance is distributed and characterized, rather than its magnitude alone, matters for instruction data selection.

Large language models are increasingly deployed in morally and legally sensitive contexts, yet little is known about how they internally represent distinctions between moral reasoning styles. Dir-A can causally change judgments, and in conflicting scenarios, it selectively corrects errors in rule-based judgments without changing consequence-based judgments, suggesting that it does not simply make the model more likely to accept everything. Speech timing is fundamental for speech models to recognize words accurately, but how word-timing information is represented in speech models remains underexplored. We study this question using the framework of representational geometry, which investigates whether and how concepts are represented in low-dimensional subspaces of the representation space. Prior work in cognitive neuroscience has shown that when HuBERT feature sequences are averaged across words of the same duration, they form near-circular trajectories from word onset to word offset in a two-dimensional "temporal subspace." Here we show that this circular structure of word timing is a general property of deep speech representations, by demonstrating its emergence in nine additional speech models covering both supervised and self-supervised. We then move beyond averaged word segments and show that in HuBERT, the circular trajectories are consistent enough at the level of individual words to perform word segmentation. Our approach, Rotary Segmentation (RoSeg), achieves 64.3% boundary F-score on Librispeech by detecting word boundaries when cycles complete in the temporal subspace. Although supervision is needed to identify a good subspace, nevertheless this result demonstrates much stronger implicit word knowledge in HuBERT than has previously been shown.

Mixed Feelings, Single Polarity
复杂情感，单一极性
Emotion datasets are routinely mapped onto positive and negative valence, by assigning each emotion category one polarity. We test where this works and where it fails, using SemEval-2018 Affect in Tweets (English, Arabic, Spanish), Affective Text aligned with EmoBank, raw GoEmotions annotations, naturalistic hashtag corpora, and a controlled annotation study. Fixed projection works well when a text carries labels of one valence. It fails on a subset identifiable from the labels alone: tweets whose emotion labels point in opposite directions. These are 9.0% of polar SemEval test tweets but cause 54.8% of the polarity errors of a learned projection, are more than twice as likely to receive a neutral-or-mixed gold label, and are not rescued by modeling the full label set. Annotators produce such configurations routinely: 16.3% of multilabel GoEmotions judgments combine emotions from the dataset's own positive and negative parents. In a controlled study holding word and reader constant, context changes the coarse valence judgment in 56.8% of cases, against 19.9% for controls. We recommend projecting label configurations rather than labels, abstaining or keeping a mixed class where labels conflict, and reporting coverage alongside accuracy.
